literature.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 人们对 疫苗接种 的态度各不相同,大约一半的参与者认为这是一种合理的预防措施。主要动机是防止禽流感病毒和人流感病毒之间的重配,而重要的障碍包括对政府的信任度降低、监管负担以及 疫苗接种 的有限益处。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10980839/v1]
主要结果表明,美国本季流行的流感 疫苗 列于表 3 中。没有报告具体的数字结果或百分比。 [10.58347/tml.2026.1765a]

严重肺炎在老年患者中更为常见,并且与较高的体重指数(BMI)、高血压、糖尿病、吸烟暴露和住院时间较长有关。与轻症病例相比,重症病例更常出现咳嗽、呼吸困难、鼻塞/鼻漏、中性粒细胞增多、淋巴细胞减少、血小板减少、eGFR降低、肌酐升高、肝酶异常、红细胞沉降率升高等症状。tNGS揭示了不同的合并感染模式:轻症病例以细菌为主,以流感嗜血杆菌为主要病原体,而重症病例的真菌合并感染率明显较高,特别是白色念珠菌和烟曲霉,并且检出更多EB病毒。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11092290/v1]
InfluProto 准确地区分了三个 宿主 类别,实现了超过 0.97 的召回率和精度,并且大大优于传统分类模型,特别是在具有挑战性的人畜共患菌株方面,包括 2009 年大流行的 H1N1 (pdm09) 谱系。 [10.64898/2026.10.07.757480]

流感季节期间所有年龄段的人群均检测到流感。7-12 岁儿童 (6.3%) 和 13-18 岁儿童 (5.2%) 的平均跨季节检出率最高。所有年龄段的残余分数相似(19.6%-25.6%)。然而,7-12 岁儿童在活跃的季间周中的检出率最高,占 42%,并且表现出最高的 lag-1 自相关性 (0.44),表明循环是持续的而不是零星的。在季节高峰后 15 周,7-12 岁的儿童保留了大约 55% 的峰值检出率,而 ≥50 岁的成人则低于 10%。 [10.1097/inf.0000000000005434]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Attitudes towards vaccination varied, with approximately half of the participants considering it a reasonable preventive measure. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10980839/v1]
The main results indicate that influenza vaccines available this season in the US are listed in Table 3. No specific numerical findings or percentages are reported. [10.58347/tml.2026.1765a]

Severe pneumonia was more common in older patients and was associated with higher body mass index (BMI), greater rates of hypertension, diabetes, smoking exposure, and longer hospitalization. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11092290/v1]

InfluProto accurately discriminated among the three host classes, achieving recall and precision exceeding 0.97, and substantially outperformed conventional classification models, particularly on challenging zoonotic strains, including the 2009 pandemic H1N1 (pdm09) lineage. [10.64898/2026.10.07.757480]

Influenza was detected during the inter-season in all age groups. Mean inter-season detection rates were highest in children 7-12 years (6.3%) and 13-18 years old (5.2%). The residual fraction was similar across all ages (19.6%-25.6%). [10.1097/inf.0000000000005434]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
人们对 疫苗接种 的态度各不相同,大约一半的参与者认为这是一种合理的预防措施。主要动机是防止禽流感病毒和人流感病毒之间的重配,而重要的障碍包括对政府的信任度降低、监管负担以及 疫苗接种 的有限益处。
主要结果表明,美国本季流行的流感 疫苗 列于表 3 中。没有报告具体的数字结果或百分比。 [10.58347/tml.2026.1765a]。

严重肺炎在老年患者中更为常见,并且与较高的体重指数(BMI)、高血压、糖尿病、吸烟暴露和住院时间较长有关。与轻症病例相比,重症病例更常出现咳嗽、呼吸困难、鼻塞/鼻漏、中性粒细胞增多、淋巴细胞减少、血小板减少、eGFR降低、肌酐升高、肝酶异常、红细胞沉降率升高等症状。tNGS揭示了不同的合并感染模式:轻症病例以细菌为主,以流感嗜血杆菌为主要病原体,而重症病例的真菌合并感染率明显较高,特别是白色念珠菌和烟曲霉,并且检出更多EB病毒。

papers.title: A qualitative study exploring poultry farmers’ barriers and motivations to seasonal human influenza vaccine uptake as a preventive public health measure because of avian influenza
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: The global spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) has increased concerns about reassortment between avian and human influenza viruses and the potential emergence of novel pandemic influenza strains. Annual seasonal influenza vaccination can reduce this risk and is recommended by the Dutch government and the World Health Organization (WHO) for risk groups, including poultry farmers. This study explored Dutch poultry farmers’ perceptions regarding this vaccination and identified motivations and barriers influencing their willingness to be vaccinated. Methods: This qualitative study involved semistructured interviews with twelve poultry farmers in the Netherlands. Interviews were conducted online via Microsoft Teams between June and October 2024. The interview guide was based on the attitude‒social influence‒self-efficacy (ASE) model. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed using thematic analysis. Results: Attitudes towards vaccination differed both generally and regarding seasonal influenza vaccination due to avian influenza risk. Approximately half considered vaccination a reasonable preventive measure. The main motivation for vaccination was preventing reassortment between avian and human influenza viruses and thereby reducing the risk of a future pandemic. Participants also viewed vaccination as a sign of societal responsibility and a way to contribute positively to the public image of the poultry sector. Important barriers included diminished trust in the government, perceived regulatory burden within the poultry sector, and perceived limited benefits of vaccination. Participants emphasized that vaccination should remain voluntary. Participants generally perceived their personal risk of avian influenza infection as low, while acknowledging potentially severe consequences for public health if a novel influenza virus were to emerge. Trusted sources of information included veterinarians, general practitioners, poultry advisers, and agricultural organizations. Accessibility was considered essential: local, flexible in timing, and free of charge. Conclusions: Acceptance of seasonal influenza vaccination among poultry farmers is influenced by a combination of societal responsibility, perceived risk, trust in the government, and practical considerations. Vaccination strategies should emphasize the societal benefits of vaccination and the potentially serious public health consequences of the emergence of a novel influenza virus. Improving vaccine uptake among poultry farmers requires engagement of trusted intermediaries and vaccination programs that are accessible and tailored to farmers’ practical needs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore poultry farmers’ perceptions of seasonal human influenza vaccination as a preventive measure against avian influenza, highlighting concerns about reassortment between avian and human influenza viruses and the risk of emerging pandemic strains.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This qualitative study involved semistructured interviews with twelve poultry farmers in the Netherlands, conducted online via Microsoft Teams between June and October 2024.
analysis.methods: The study used semistructured interviews guided by the attitude‒social influence‒self-efficacy (ASE) model, which were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using thematic analysis.
analysis.main_results: Attitudes towards vaccination varied, with approximately half of the participants considering it a reasonable preventive measure. The main motivation was preventing reassortment between avian and human influenza viruses, while important barriers included diminished trust in the government, perceived regulatory burden, and perceived limited benefits of vaccination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that vaccination acceptance among poultry farmers is influenced by a combination of societal responsibility, perceived risk, trust in the government, and practical considerations, offering a novel insight into the factors affecting vaccine uptake in this specific group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform public health strategies by emphasizing the need for vaccination programs that highlight societal benefits and the potential public health consequences of novel influenza virus emergence, while also addressing practical barriers to uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce bias. However, the evidence is strong given the detailed thematic analysis and the inclusion of multiple perspectives from poultry farmers.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the perceptions of Dutch poultry farmers regarding seasonal human influenza vaccination as a preventive measure against avian influenza. The research highlights the importance of societal responsibility, perceived risk, and practical considerations in influencing vaccine uptake. The findings suggest that vaccination strategies should emphasize the public health benefits and address barriers such as lack of trust in government and perceived limited benefits. The study, based on semistructured interviews with twelve farmers, provides a nuanced understanding of motivations and challenges related to vaccine acceptance. While the small sample size and self-reported data limit the generalizability of the results, the thematic analysis offers a robust interpretation of the factors affecting vaccine uptake in this group. The results have implications for public health by informing the development of more effective vaccination programs tailored to the needs of poultry farmers.

papers.title_zh: 一项定性研究,探讨家禽养殖户将季节性人类流感 疫苗 作为禽流感预防性公共卫生措施的障碍和动机
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background: The global spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) has increased concerns about reassortment between avian and human influenza viruses and the potential emergence of novel pandemic influenza strains. Annual seasonal influenza vaccination can reduce this risk and is recommended by the Dutch government and the World Health Organization (WHO) for risk groups, including poultry farmers. This study explored Dutch poultry farmers’ perceptions regarding this vaccination and identified motivations and barriers influencing their willingness to be vaccinated. Methods: This qualitative study involved semistructured interviews with twelve poultry farmers in the Netherlands. Interviews were conducted online via Microsoft Teams between June and October 2024. The interview guide was based on the attitude‒social influence‒self-efficacy (ASE) model. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed using thematic analysis. Results: Attitudes towards vaccination differed both generally and regarding seasonal influenza vaccination due to avian influenza risk. Approximately half considered vaccination a reasonable preventive measure. The main motivation for vaccination was preventing reassortment between avian and human influenza viruses and thereby reducing the risk of a future pandemic. Participants also viewed vaccination as a sign of societal responsibility and a way to contribute positively to the public image of the poultry sector. Important barriers included diminished trust in the government, perceived regulatory burden within the poultry sector, and perceived limited benefits of vaccination. Participants emphasized that vaccination should remain voluntary. Participants generally perceived their personal risk of avian influenza infection as low, while acknowledging potentially severe consequences for public health if a novel influenza virus were to emerge. Trusted sources of information included veterinarians, general practitioners, poultry advisers, and agricultural organizations. Accessibility was considered essential: local, flexible in timing, and free of charge. Conclusions: Acceptance of seasonal influenza vaccination among poultry farmers is influenced by a combination of societal responsibility, perceived risk, trust in the government, and practical considerations. Vaccination strategies should emphasize the societal benefits of vaccination and the potentially serious public health consequences of the emergence of a novel influenza virus. Improving vaccine uptake among poultry farmers requires engagement of trusted intermediaries and vaccination programs that are accessible and tailored to farmers’ practical needs.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景:高致病性禽流感(H5N1)的全球传播增加了人们对禽流感病毒和人流感病毒重配以及可能出现新型大流行流感毒株的担忧。每年一次的 季节性流感 疫苗接种 可以降低这种风险,是荷兰政府和世界卫生组织 (WHO) 建议风险群体(包括家禽养殖户)使用的。本研究探讨了荷兰家禽养殖户对 疫苗接种 的看法,并确定了影响他们接种疫苗意愿的动机和障碍。方法:这项定性研究涉及对荷兰 12 名家禽养殖户的半结构化访谈。面试于 2024 年 6 月至 10 月期间通过 Microsoft Teams 在线进行。面试指南基于态度-社会影响力-自我效能 (ASE) 模型。访谈内容逐字记录并使用主题分析进行分析。结果:由于禽流感风险,人们对 疫苗接种 的态度总体上和对 季节性流感 疫苗接种 的态度都不同。大约一半的人认为 疫苗接种 是合理的预防措施。疫苗接种 的主要动机是防止禽流感病毒和人流感病毒之间的重配,从而降低未来大流行的风险。参与者还将 疫苗接种 视为社会责任的标志,也是为家禽行业公众形象做出积极贡献的一种方式。重要的障碍包括对政府的信任度下降、家禽行业的监管负担以及 疫苗接种 的好处有限。与会者强调,疫苗接种 应保持自愿。参与者普遍认为自己感染禽流感的风险较低,同时也承认如果出现新型流感病毒,可能会对公共健康造成严重后果。值得信赖的信息来源包括兽医、全科医生、家禽顾问和农业组织。无障碍被认为是至关重要的:本地化、时间灵活且免费。结论:家禽养殖户对 季节性流感 疫苗接种 的接受程度受到社会责任、感知风险、对政府的信任和实际考虑的综合影响。疫苗接种 策略应强调 疫苗接种 的社会效益以及新型流感病毒的出现可能造成的严重公共卫生后果。提高家禽养殖户对 疫苗 的采用需要值得信赖的中介机构和 疫苗接种 计划的参与,这些计划可以访问并根据农民的实际需求量身定制。

papers.title: InfluProto: Predicting Cross-Species Transmission of Influenza A Virus via Prototype Learning
papers.abstract: Zoonotic influenza A viruses pose constitute a significant persistent threat to global public health, yet quantitative approaches for assessing their cross-species transmission potential remain limited. Here, we present InfluProto, a deep learning model that introduces prototype learning into host prediction for influenza A virus, framing conceptualizing host adaptation as a continuous process rather than a discrete outcome. InfluProto embeds viral sequences into a continuous representation space anchored by human, swine, and avian prototypes, using cosine distances as a quantitative measure of host adaptation. InfluProto accurately discriminated among the three host classes, achieving recall and precision exceeding 0.97, and substantially outperformed conventional classification models models—particularly on challenging zoonotic strains, including the 2009 pandemic H1N1 (pdm09) lineage. Beyond host classification, the learned representations captured biologically meaningful host-adaptive signatures,; notably, with pdm09 viruses occupying occupied an intermediate position between human and swine clusters, consistent with their evolutionary origin. Analysis of simulated reassortment further revealed that the introduction of human–origin segments into swine influenza viruses reduced their distance to the human prototype, indicating that InfluProto can detect reassortment-associated shifts in host adaptation. To facilitate broad public useaccess, we have developed an interactive web service for InfluProto. Collectively, our work establishes a continuous framework for characterizing host adaptation and evaluating zoonotic risk in influenza A viruses, with potential implications for pandemic surveillance and preparedness.

papers.title: School-age Children as the Dominant Source of Inter-seasonal Influenza Circulation in the Republic of Korea, 2022–2025
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza circulates at low levels during summer inter-seasonal periods, potentially bridging consecutive epidemics. Which age groups contribute most to this residual circulation is not well characterized. METHODS: We analyzed weekly influenza detection rates from the Korea Sentinel Surveillance System (K-SenS), stratified by 6 age groups, from 2022 to 2025 (209 weeks). The inter-season was defined as epidemiologic weeks 21-39. For each age group, we calculated the mean inter-season detection rate, the residual fraction (inter-season rate/season rate), dominance weeks (weeks with the highest detection rate), lag-1 autocorrelation of weekly rates and normalized post-peak decay curves. RESULTS: Influenza was detected during the inter-season in all age groups. Mean inter-season detection rates were highest in children 7-12 years (6.3%) and 13-18 years old (5.2%). The residual fraction was similar across all ages (19.6%-25.6%). However, children 7-12 years old had the highest detection rate in 42% of active inter-season weeks and showed the highest lag-1 autocorrelation (0.44), indicating sustained rather than sporadic circulation. At 15 weeks after the season peak, children 7-12 years of age retained approximately 55% of their peak detection rate, compared with below 10% in adults ≥50 years old. CONCLUSIONS: School-age children, particularly those 7-12 years of age, were the dominant source of inter-seasonal influenza circulation in Korea. Their dominance was driven by high seasonal burden rather than slower viral clearance. Maintaining high vaccination coverage in this age group may help reduce inter-seasonal virus reservoirs.

source_records.abstract: BACKGROUND Influenza circulates at low levels during summer inter-seasonal periods, potentially bridging consecutive epidemics. Which age groups contribute most to this residual circulation is not well characterized. METHODS We analyzed weekly influenza detection rates from the Korea Sentinel Surveillance System (K-SenS), stratified by 6 age groups, from 2022 to 2025 (209 weeks). The inter-season was defined as epidemiologic weeks 21-39. For each age group, we calculated the mean inter-season detection rate, the residual fraction (inter-season rate/season rate), dominance weeks (weeks with the highest detection rate), lag-1 autocorrelation of weekly rates and normalized post-peak decay curves. RESULTS Influenza was detected during the inter-season in all age groups. Mean inter-season detection rates were highest in children 7-12 years (6.3%) and 13-18 years old (5.2%). The residual fraction was similar across all ages (19.6%-25.6%). However, children 7-12 years old had the highest detection rate in 42% of active inter-season weeks and showed the highest lag-1 autocorrelation (0.44), indicating sustained rather than sporadic circulation. At 15 weeks after the season peak, children 7-12 years of age retained approximately 55% of their peak detection rate, compared with below 10% in adults ≥50 years old. Their dominance was driven by high seasonal burden rather than slower viral clearance. Maintaining high vaccination coverage in this age group may help reduce inter-seasonal virus reservoirs.

papers.title: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases in the Sahel: a One Health investigation of an influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 outbreak in the Abéché Health District, Chad, 2021
papers.abstract: Emerging infectious diseases threaten global health security, particularly where integrated human-animal-environment surveillance is limited. In May 2021, Chad reported an influenza-like illness (ILI) outbreak in the Abéché Health District (Ouaddaï Province) following unusual avian mortality. We conducted a One Health investigation from May 1 to June 24, 2021, combining active case finding, a neighborhood-matched case-control study (58 cases, 58 controls) of warthog- and poultry-related exposures, an animal/environmental investigation, and virological testing (quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction [RT-qPCR] in humans; hemagglutination inhibition in poultry). We identified 210 ILI cases, 77.6% in the Amtiab villages (Abéché Health District); children under 10 were the most affected, with one death (probable encephalitis, age 13). Age under 15 years (odds ratio [OR]=4.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.61-12.55) and contact with a case (OR=4.39, 95% CI: 1.89-10.21) were significantly associated with ILI. RT-qPCR confirmed A(H1N1)pdm09 in humans; poultry showed prior mortality and anti-H9N2 antibodies, without an established causal link. This investigation rapidly identified an A(H1N1)pdm09 outbreak in a rural Sahelian setting where human-wildlife-poultry cohabitation and poor sanitation favor zoonotic pathogens. Young age and close contact drove the transmission. Strengthened integrated influenza surveillance and diagnostic capacity are needed in sub-Saharan Africa.
papers.journal: Sahelian Journal of Responsible One Health

papers.title: Seasonal influenza vaccination among healthcare workers in Lebanese hospitals: determinants of uptake post-COVID-19 pandemic and economic crisis
papers.abstract: Background Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased risk of acquiring and transmitting influenza. We assessed self-reported influenza vaccination uptake among surveyed HCWs in Lebanese hospitals during 2023–2024, compared it with their reported uptake in pre-pandemic 2018–2019, and identified factors associated with non-vaccination. Methods This cross-sectional survey was conducted from April to July 2024 among HCWs from 14 public and private hospitals across multiple regions of Lebanon. The questionnaire assessed influenza vaccination status, free institutional vaccine provision, awareness, attitudes, and COVID-19 vaccine–related perceptions. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with non-vaccination in 2023–2024. Results Among 391 participants, self-reported influenza vaccination uptake was lower in 2023–2024 than in 2018–2019 (29.9% vs 60.5%, p < 0.0001). Free institutional vaccine provision was also lower (39.6% vs 70.1%, p < 0.0001), and 19.2% were willing to pay out of pocket. Higher odds of non-vaccination were observed among HCWs aged <30 years (aOR 3.80, 95% CI 1.96–7.68), non-physicians (aOR 5.17, 95% CI 2.26–12.42), those without free institutional vaccine provision (aOR 17.74, 95% CI 9.38–35.72), those with unfavorable influenza vaccination attitudes (aOR 4.61, 95% CI 2.10–10.63), and those with moderate-to-high COVID-19 vaccine–related hesitancy (aOR 2.09, 95% CI 1.03–4.27). Conclusion Among surveyed HCWs, influenza vaccination uptake in 2023–2024 was substantially lower than reported for 2018–2019. Lack of free institutional vaccine provision and unfavorable vaccine-related perceptions were independently associated with non-vaccination. Restoring free workplace-based vaccination and addressing COVID-19 vaccine–related hesitancy may improve uptake in resource-constrained healthcare settings.

It found a significant decline in vaccination rates, with 29.9% of HCWs vaccinated in 2023–2024 versus 60.5% in 2018–2019. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 医护人员 (HCW) 感染和传播流感的风险增加。该研究旨在评估 2023 年至 2024 年黎巴嫩医院医护人员对流感 疫苗接种 的吸收情况,并将其与大流行前的 2018 年至 2019 年数据进行比较,以确定与非 疫苗接种 相关的因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面调查于 2024 年 4 月至 7 月在黎巴嫩多个地区的 14 家公立和私立医院的医护人员中进行。该研究共有 391 名参与者。
elements_zh.methods: 该调查问卷评估了流感 疫苗接种 状态、免费机构 疫苗 提供、意识、态度和 COVID-19 疫苗 相关认知。多变量逻辑回归确定了 2023-2024 年与非 疫苗接种 独立相关的因素。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在年龄 <30 岁的医护人员、非医生、没有免费机构 疫苗 服务的人员、对流感 疫苗接种 持不利态度的人员以及具有中度至高度的 COVID-19 疫苗 相关犹豫的人员中,观察到非 疫苗接种 的几率较高。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,恢复基于工作场所的免费 疫苗接种 并解决 疫苗 犹豫问题可以提高资源有限的医疗机构中流感 疫苗接种 的吸收率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于自我报告的数据,这可能会引入回忆偏差。由于横截面设计和对调查答复的依赖,证据的强度适中。

papers.title: Mutational fitness landscapes of diverse human influenza H1N1 neuraminidases
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT While neuraminidase (NA) is emerging as a promising influenza vaccine target, it evolves rapidly and undergoes antigenic drift. However, our understanding of its evolutionary constraints remains limited. Here, we systematically quantified the replication fitness effects of >6,000 mutations for each of three antigenically diverse H1N1 NAs using deep mutational scanning. Moderate correlations among H1N1 NA fitness landscapes revealed mutations with strain-dependent replication fitness effects. Additionally, cross-subtype comparison between N1 and N2 NAs uncovered similar epistatic effects that were enriched in the C-terminal interprotomer interface. We also showed that NA mutational fitness strongly correlated between in vivo and in vitro . Characterization of 40 individually constructed NA mutants further demonstrated that NA mutational fitness depended more on its surface protein expression than on its total protein expression or endoplasmic reticulum stress induction. Overall, the large dataset generated in this work provides critical insights into the evolutionary constraints of NA.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study systematically quantified the replication fitness effects of over 6,000 mutations for three antigenically diverse H1N1 NAs using deep mutational scanning.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed deep mutational scanning to assess the replication fitness effects of mutations in H1N1 neuraminidases, comparing in vivo and in vitro results and constructing individual NA mutants for further analysis.
analysis.main_results: Moderate correlations among H1N1 NA fitness landscapes were observed, revealing mutations with strain-dependent replication fitness effects. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide novel insights into the evolutionary constraints of NA, highlighting the importance of surface protein expression in determining mutational fitness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform the development of more effective influenza vaccines and antiviral strategies by elucidating the factors that influence NA mutational fitness and antigenic drift.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's large dataset offers high confidence, but its focus on H1N1 NAs may limit generalizability to other influenza subtypes or lineages.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mutational fitness landscapes of three antigenically diverse H1N1 neuraminidases (NAs) to better understand their evolutionary constraints. Using deep mutational scanning, the researchers quantified the replication fitness effects of over 6,000 mutations, revealing moderate correlations among H1N1 NA fitness landscapes and strain-dependent effects. Cross-subtype comparisons between N1 and N2 NAs uncovered similar epistatic effects concentrated in the C-terminal interprotomer interface. The study also demonstrated strong correlations between in vivo and in vitro NA mutational fitness. These findings highlight the role of surface protein expression in determining NA fitness and provide critical insights for vaccine and antiviral development. The large dataset supports high confidence, though the results may not be fully generalizable to other influenza subtypes.

papers.title: Targeted Next-Generation Sequencing Reveals Co-infection Patterns and Risk Factors for Severe Pneumonia in Influenza A(H1N1) pdm09
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 remains a major cause of seasonal respiratory morbidity, yet predictors of progression to severe pneumonia and the associated co-infection profile remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe the clinical features, laboratory abnormalities, pathogen spectrum, and risk factors for severe influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia using targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS). Methods In this retrospective single-center study, hospitalized patients admitted to Panyu Central Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University between January and December 2024 were analyzed. Based on tNGS and clinical classification, 175 patients infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 were included, comprising 92 mild cases and 83 severe pneumonia cases; 121 non-H1N1 respiratory infection cases served as controls. Demographic data, symptoms, comorbidities, blood routine and biochemical indices, and co-infection profiles were compared. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify risk factors for severe disease. Results Severe pneumonia was more common in older patients and was associated with higher body mass index (BMI), greater rates of hypertension, diabetes, smoking exposure, and longer hospitalization. Compared with mild cases, severe cases showed more frequent cough, dyspnea, nasal congestion/rhinorrhea, neutrophilia, lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced eGFR, elevated creatinine, liver enzyme abnormalities, and increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate. tNGS revealed distinct co-infection patterns: mild cases were predominantly bacterial, with Haemophilus influenzae as the leading pathogen, whereas severe cases had significantly higher fungal co-infection rates, particularly Candida albicans and Aspergillus fumigatus, and more Epstein-Barr virus detection. In multivariate analysis, age, BMI, cough, dyspnea, and nasal congestion/rhinorrhea were independent risk factors for severe pneumonia, while headache was protective. Conclusion Severe influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia is characterized by advanced age, elevated BMI, respiratory symptoms, systemic inflammation, organ dysfunction, and a shift toward fungal/viral co-infection. Early risk stratification and pathogen-directed management may improve outcomes in high-risk patients.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 仍然是季节性呼吸道疾病的主要原因,但进展为严重肺炎的预测因素以及相关的合并感染特征仍未完全确定。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在利用靶向下一代测序(tNGS)描述重症流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 肺炎的临床特征、实验室异常、病原体谱和危险因素。在这项回顾性单中心研究中,对2024年1月至12月广州医科大学番禺中心医院收治的住院患者进行了分析。
elements_zh.methods: 根据tNGS和临床分型,纳入175例流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09感染患者,其中轻症92例,重症肺炎83例;121例非H1N1呼吸道感染病例作为对照。使用单变量和多变量逻辑回归来确定严重疾病的危险因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 严重肺炎在老年患者中更为常见,并且与较高的体重指数(BMI)、高血压、糖尿病、吸烟暴露和住院时间较长有关。与轻症病例相比,重症病例更常出现咳嗽、呼吸困难、鼻塞/鼻漏、中性粒细胞增多、淋巴细胞减少、血小板减少、eGFR降低、肌酐升高、肝酶异常、红细胞沉降率升高等症状。tNGS揭示了不同的合并感染模式:轻症病例以细菌为主,以流感嗜血杆菌为主要病原体,而重症病例的真菌合并感染率明显较高,特别是白色念珠菌和烟曲霉,并且检出更多EB病毒。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 多变量分析显示,年龄、BMI、咳嗽、呼吸困难和鼻塞/鼻漏是重症肺炎的独立危险因素,而头痛具有保护作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 早期风险分层和针对病原体的管理可能会改善高危患者的预后。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告局限性。

papers.title: Maternal Influenza Infection During Pregnancy and Neuropsychiatric Disorders in Offspring
papers.abstract: Importance: Evidence on maternal influenza infection during pregnancy and offspring neuropsychiatric risk remains inconsistent and limited by methodologic concerns. Objective: To evaluate the association of maternal influenza infection during pregnancy and offspring neuropsychiatric risk. Design, Setting, and Participants: This binational cohort study included mother-child pairs from the National Health Insurance Service birth cohort in South Korea (discovery cohort) and the JMDC (previously Japan Medical Data Center) birth cohort in Japan (replication cohort). Children born between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2017, were included in the study and followed up until December 31, 2023. Exposure: A first recorded maternal influenza diagnosis during pregnancy. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was first postnatal diagnosis of any neuropsychiatric disorder in offspring, including severe neuropsychiatric disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorder, and intellectual disability. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to adjust for confounding. Weighted Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) and 95% CIs. Subgroup analyses were conducted by trimester and season of infection, and sibling-comparison analyses used exposure-discordant sibling pairs. Data analysis was performed from September 2025 to July 2026. Results: The discovery cohort included 2 564 435 mother-child pairs (mean [SD] maternal age, 31.9 [4.1] years; 1 293 773 [50.5%] male offspring), of whom 35 973 (1.4%) were exposed to maternal influenza during pregnancy. The replication cohort included 181 681 pairs (92 738 [51.0%] male offspring), of whom 11 198 (6.2%) were exposed. In stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting-based analyses, maternal influenza infection was associated with an increased risk of any neuropsychiatric disorder in the discovery cohort (AHR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.04-1.14) and replication cohort (AHR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.02-1.19). Sibling-comparison analyses included 33 191 and 7842 mother-child pairs in the discovery and replication cohorts, respectively; there was not a statistically significant association in the discovery cohort (AHR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.89-1.09) and replication cohort (AHR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.88-1.22). Conclusions and Relevance: In this binational cohort study of mother-child pairs in South Korea and Japan, the modest population-level association between maternal influenza infection during pregnancy and the risk of any neuropsychiatric disorder in offspring was attenuated and not statistically significant in sibling-comparison analyses in either cohort. These findings suggest that familial factors may account for the association observed in the population-level analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between maternal influenza infection during pregnancy and the risk of neuropsychiatric disorders in offspring using binational cohort data from South Korea and Japan. The discovery cohort included 2,564,435 mother-child pairs, with 35,973 exposed to maternal influenza, while the replication cohort had 181,681 pairs, of whom 11,198 were exposed. Using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting, the study found a modest increased risk of neuropsychiatric disorders in offspring exposed to maternal influenza, with adjusted hazard ratios of 1.09 (95% CI, 1.04-1.14) and 1.10 (95% CI, 1.02-1.19) in the discovery and replication cohorts, respectively. However, sibling-comparison analyses showed no statistically significant association, suggesting potential confounding by familial factors. The study's findings imply that while there may be a population-level link, the relationship is not necessarily causal and may require further investigation. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the limitations in establishing causality.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估孕期母亲流感感染与后代神经精神风险之间的关系,因为该主题的证据仍然不一致,并且受到方法学问题的限制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项双边 队列研究 研究包括韩国国民健康保险服务出生 队列研究(发现 队列研究)和日本 JMDC 出生 队列研究(复制 队列研究)的母子对。2010年1月1日至2017年12月31日期间出生的儿童被纳入研究,并随访至2023年12月31日。
elements_zh.methods: 加权 Cox 比例风险模型估计调整后的风险比 (AHR) 和 95% CI。应用 治疗 加权的稳定逆概率来调整混杂因素。按妊娠期和感染季节进行亚组分析,并使用暴露不一致的兄弟姐妹对进行兄弟姐妹比较分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在基于稳定逆概率治疗加权分析的模型中,妊娠期间母亲流感感染与发现队列研究中后代任何神经精神疾病风险增加相关(AHR为1.09;95% CI为1.04-1.14),以及复制队列研究中相关(AHR为1.10;95% CI为1.02-1.19)。兄弟姐妹比较分析显示,发现队列研究和复制队列研究中均未发现统计学显著关联(AHR分别为0.98;95% CI为0.89-1.09和1.04;95% CI为0.88-1.22)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,家庭因素可能解释了人群水平分析中观察到的关联,表明孕产妇流感感染与后代神经精神疾病之间的关系可能不是因果关系。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能为 监测 和孕期母亲流感感染的风险评估策略及其对后代神经精神健康的潜在影响提供信息,强调需要进一步研究家庭影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的人群水平关联在兄弟姐妹比较分析中被削弱,表明存在潜在的混杂因素。由于依赖观察数据并且需要进一步的因果调查,证据是中等的。

papers.abstract_zh: 重要性:关于妊娠期间母亲流感感染与后代神经精神疾病风险的证据仍不一致且受到方法学问题的限制。目的:评估妊娠期间母亲流感感染与后代神经精神疾病风险的关联。设计、地点和参与者:这项跨国队列研究研究包括来自韩国国家健康保险服务出生队列研究(发现队列研究)和日本JMDC(原日本医疗数据中心)出生队列研究(复制队列研究)的母子对。研究纳入了2010年1月1日至2017年12月31日出生的儿童,并随访至2023年12月31日。暴露:妊娠期间首次记录的母亲流感诊断。主要结局和测量指标:主要结局是后代任何神经精神疾病的首次产后诊断,包括严重的神经精神疾病、强迫症、注意力缺陷/多动障碍、自闭症谱系障碍和智力残疾。采用稳定逆概率治疗加权分析来调整混杂因素。加权Cox比例风险模型估计了调整后的风险比(AHRs)和95%置信区间(CI)。进行了按感染孕周和季节的亚组分析,并使用暴露不一致的兄弟姐妹对进行兄弟姐妹比较分析。数据分析于2025年9月至2026年7月进行。结果:发现队列研究包括2,564,435对母子(母亲平均年龄[标准差]为31.9[4.1]岁;1,293,773[50.5%]名男性后代),其中35,973(1.4%)对在妊娠期间暴露于母亲流感感染。复制队列研究包括181,681对母子(其中92,738[51.0%]名男性后代),其中11,198(6.2%)对暴露于母亲流感感染。在基于稳定逆概率治疗加权分析的模型中,妊娠期间母亲流感感染与发现队列研究中后代任何神经精神疾病风险增加相关(AHR为1.09;95% CI为1.04-1.14),以及复制队列研究中相关(AHR为1.10;95% CI为1.02-1.19)。兄弟姐妹比较分析包括发现队列研究中的33,191对和复制队列研究中的7,842对母子;在发现队列研究中未发现统计学显著关联(AHR为0.98;95% CI为0.89-1.09),在复制队列研究中也未发现统计学显著关联(AHR为1.04;95% CI为0.88-1.22)。结论和相关性:在这项涉及韩国和日本母子对的跨国队列研究研究中,妊娠期间母亲流感感染与后代任何神经精神疾病风险之间存在适度的群体水平关联,但在发现队列研究和复制队列研究的兄弟姐妹比较分析中,该关联被减弱且不具有统计学显著性。这些发现表明,家族因素可能解释了群体水平分析中观察到的关联。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估孕期母亲流感感染与后代神经精神风险之间的关系,因为该主题的证据仍然不一致,并且受到方法学问题的限制。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项双边 队列研究 研究包括韩国国民健康保险服务出生 队列研究(发现 队列研究)和日本 JMDC 出生 队列研究(复制 队列研究)的母子对。2010年1月1日至2017年12月31日期间出生的儿童被纳入研究,并随访至2023年12月31日。
analysis_zh.methods: 加权 Cox 比例风险模型估计调整后的风险比 (AHR) 和 95% CI。应用 治疗 加权的稳定逆概率来调整混杂因素。按妊娠期和感染季节进行亚组分析,并使用暴露不一致的兄弟姐妹对进行兄弟姐妹比较分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在基于稳定逆概率治疗加权分析的模型中,妊娠期间母亲流感感染与发现队列研究中后代任何神经精神疾病风险增加相关(AHR为1.09;95% CI为1.04-1.14),以及复制队列研究中相关(AHR为1.10;95% CI为1.02-1.19)。兄弟姐妹比较分析显示,发现队列研究和复制队列研究中均未发现统计学显著关联(AHR分别为0.98;95% CI为0.89-1.09和1.04;95% CI为0.88-1.22)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,家庭因素可能解释了人群水平分析中观察到的关联,表明孕产妇流感感染与后代神经精神疾病之间的关系可能不是因果关系。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能为 监测 和孕期母亲流感感染的风险评估策略及其对后代神经精神健康的潜在影响提供信息,强调需要进一步研究家庭影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的人群水平关联在兄弟姐妹比较分析中被削弱,表明存在潜在的混杂因素。由于依赖观察数据并且需要进一步的因果调查,证据是中等的。

papers.full_text: AbstractSeasonal epidemics, zoonotic spillover, antiviral resistance, and pandemic risk continue to make influenza a major challenge for respiratory preparedness. The recent spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in mammalian hosts has made it increasingly important to consider molecular adaptation, surveillance, treatment, and vaccination as connected parts of preparedness rather than as separate issues. This review focuses on four interconnected areas: host–virus interactions, surveillance technologies, antiviral management and resistance, and vaccine preparedness. Evidence on mammalian adaptation includes receptor specificity, viral polymerase–host factor compatibility, innate immune antagonism, ANP32 proteins, and aberrant viral RNA generation, while surveillance has expanded to multiplex and CRISPR-based assays, point-of-care platforms, genomic sequencing, artificial intelligence-assisted risk assessment, and environmental monitoring. These approaches differ in intended use and stage of validation. Antiviral benefit depends strongly on host risk and treatment timing. Resistance-associated substitutions, however, cannot be interpreted from sequence data alone and require phenotypic and epidemiological context. Vaccine development spans nanoparticle, mRNA, and intranasal platforms designed to broaden antigenic coverage, strengthen mucosal immunity, or improve protection in specific populations. Better analytical performance and stronger immune responses do not by themselves demonstrate reductions in severe disease, hospitalization, or mortality. Influenza preparedness ultimately depends on how effectively these four domains inform one another and how consistently emerging approaches are evaluated against clinically meaningful outcomes.Keywords: antiviral resistance, emerging respiratory threats, host–virus interactions, influenza virus, surveillance technologies, vaccine preparedness Graphical abstract The central figure represents the host/patient. The surrounding modules summarize viral threats, pathogenic mechanisms, diagnostic and surveillance approaches, epidemiology and risk stratification, clinical management and recovery, and vaccine development. Examples shown include H5N1 threats; M1, NS2, mvRNA, and RIG-I-related mechanisms; multiplex PCR and CRISPR-based diagnostics; AI-assisted and wastewater surveillance; smartwatch-based recovery assessment; and COBRA, nanoparticle, and mRNA vaccine platforms. The converging arrows indicate the translational focus of the review: using information from these domains to improve protection of human health.Conceptual diagram illustrating host-virus interaction at the center, surrounded by six labeled sections: vaccine development, viral threats, mechanisms and immunity, diagnostics and technologies, epidemiology and surveillance, and treatment, each with icons and relevant keywords summarizing advancements, challenges, and monitoring strategies in influenza research. 7.DiscussionThe evidence reviewed here points to a series of translational handoffs across the four domains. Molecular findings need confirmation in human-derived systems, and surveillance signals need enough standardization to support action. Antiviral susceptibility data require phenotypic and treatment context. Vaccine-induced immune responses must ultimately be assessed against clinically meaningful outcomes. Weakness at any transition can reduce the preparedness value of an otherwise promising approach.Mammalian adaptation shows the distance between mechanistic insight and practical risk assessment. Receptor usage, viral polymerase regulation, ANP32-family proteins, NS1/NS2 function, and aberrant viral RNA generation have refined current models of cross-species adaptation. Much of the evidence still derives from structural studies, cultured cells, or animal models. Human infection adds variables such as age, pre-existing immunity, immunosenescence, fever, and other physiological conditions that can alter viral replication and host responses. Molecular adaptation markers remain candidate risk indicators until supported by human-derived experimental systems, clinical cohorts, and epidemiological evidence.Surveillance signals vary in scale, source, and validation endpoint. Multiplex assays, CRISPR-based platforms, genomic sequencing, AI-assisted analysis, and wastewater monitoring cannot be judged by a single criterion. Sampling procedures, analytical thresholds, and reporting practices add further variation. Wastewater detection of A(H5N1) is especially difficult to interpret because viral material may reflect human shedding, infected animals, or animal waste. Environmental findings are most informative when combined with clinical testing, genomic characterization, epidemiological investigation, and veterinary surveillance within a One Health framework.Clinical management has a similar interpretive constraint. A resistance-associated sequence change is not synonymous with clinical resistance. Phenotypic susceptibility, antiviral exposure, viral subtype, fitness, and treatment outcome remain necessary for judging its significance. Host-directed and TCM-derived interventions are harder to compare because study design, intervention standardization, and quality control vary. Wearable monitoring may capture longitudinal recovery patterns, but useful clinical thresholds and incremental benefit over routine assessment have not been established. These adjunctive and monitoring approaches remain investigational.Vaccine studies make the gap between immune readouts and clinical benefit especially clear. COBRA antigens, nanoparticle vaccines, mRNA platforms, and intranasal approaches address antigenic mismatch, manufacturing speed, or weak mucosal immunity. Broader antibody responses or higher neutralizing titers do not necessarily mean fewer hospitalizations or less severe disease. In older or immunocompromised populations, immunosenescence and impaired cellular immunity can weaken the relationship between serological responses and protection. Evaluation should include humoral, cellular, and mucosal responses, durability, and clinically meaningful outcomes in the intended population.Influenza preparedness depends on how these links function in practice. Evidence of viral adaptation can inform surveillance and risk assessment, and surveillance can guide clinical and public-health responses. Antiviral use generates information relevant to resistance monitoring. Viral evolution and changing population immunity influence vaccine development and updating. Standardized validation, transparent evidence grading, interoperable data sharing, and evaluation in high-risk populations are needed throughout the pathway. During seasonal epidemics, zoonotic outbreaks, or pandemics, the reliability of these links may matter more than the performance of any single technology. 1.IntroductionThe Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 analysis estimated 2.50 million (95% uncertainty interval [UI], 2.24–2.81 million) lower respiratory infection (LRI) deaths worldwide in 2023 and approximately 22.5 million (19.6–26.5 million) LRI episodes attributable to influenza (GBD 2023 Lower Respiratory Infections and Antimicrobial Resistance Collaborators, 2026). Seasonal influenza remains a substantial component of the global respiratory-disease burden. At the same time, changes in influenza ecology, host range, and the circulation of other respiratory viruses have increased the importance of preparedness for zoonotic as well as seasonal threats.Recent A(H5N1) activity provides a concrete example. Between March 2024 and May 2025, 70 human A(H5N1) infections were reported in the United States, mostly after exposure to infected dairy cattle or poultry; one fatal infection was linked to backyard poultry exposure (Rolfes et al., 2025). Infection of cats with highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in South Korea provides additional evidence of the expanding mammalian host range (Kang et al., 2024). Continued circulation in mammals creates opportunities for further adaptation, so assessment of emerging influenza risk requires molecular information to be interpreted alongside One Health surveillance, clinical risk, antiviral preparedness, and vaccine development.The difficulty is not a lack of recent advances in influenza virology, diagnostics, treatment, resistance surveillance, or vaccination, but the gap between performance in one domain and useful outcomes in another. Findings from cell or animal models may not predict human transmissibility or severity. Low analytical detection limits do not establish clinical utility, sequence-detected resistance markers do not by themselves establish clinically meaningful resistance, and stronger vaccine immunogenicity does not guarantee fewer severe outcomes. These limits are especially important when evidence is applied to older adults, immunocompromised patients, or populations exposed to emerging zoonotic viruses.The review therefore follows four linked dimensions of influenza preparedness: (1) viral and host determinants of replication, mammalian adaptation, and immune responses; (2) multi-layer surveillance for early detection and risk assessment; (3) antiviral treatment, stewardship, and resistance monitoring; and (4) vaccine strategies for broad, durable, and population-specific protection. Epidemiological risk groups, clinical outcomes, and emerging technologies are included only when they inform at least one of these domains. They are not treated as additional pillars. This structure links mechanistic evidence with surveillance, therapeutic decisions, resistance monitoring, and vaccine preparedness in a single narrative.1.1.Literature search strategyPubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for influenza studies published mainly from 2021 through 2026. Initial mapping used the broad concept “influenza,” followed by title-and-abstract screening. The narrative synthesis was limited to four preparedness-oriented domains: host–virus interactions, surveillance and diagnostic technologies, antiviral treatment and resistance, and vaccine preparedness. Earlier publications were retained when they provided essential mechanistic or clinical context. Priority was given to original research, clinical studies, large observational cohorts, surveillance reports, and publications from major public-health organizations. 1.1.Literature search strategyPubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for influenza studies published mainly from 2021 through 2026. Initial mapping used the broad concept “influenza,” followed by title-and-abstract screening. The narrative synthesis was limited to four preparedness-oriented domains: host–virus interactions, surveillance and diagnostic technologies, antiviral treatment and resistance, and vaccine preparedness. Earlier publications were retained when they provided essential mechanistic or clinical context. Priority was given to original research, clinical studies, large observational cohorts, surveillance reports, and publications from major public-health organizations. 2.Pathogenic mechanisms and host immunityInfluenza virus pathogenicity arises from complex host–virus interactions. Recent studies have revealed key mechanisms regulating viral replication, host immunity, and tissue repair (Figure 1).Figure 1Schematic of influenza A virus pathogenesis, host immunity, immunopathology, and tissue repair. The diagram is divided into four quadrants around the virus. Top left: viral entry (lateral diffusion, clathrin recruitment, membrane protrusion, endocytosis) and replication regulation (M1, NS2, ANP32B, fever-induced mvRNA/RIG-I). Top right: host immune responses, including innate activation (ARRDC4/FBP/NF-κB, HSPA1L/NA ubiquitination, neutrophil NET/ROS) and nasal immune quiescence (IRF3↓, low IFN, reversible by exogenous IFN). Bottom left: immunopathology, including severe influenza-associated immune alterations (reduced MAIT-cell responses, increased NK-cell activity, and altered memory B/T-cell responses), aging-related CD8+ T-cell defects, the aged lung PDLIM2/NF-κB axis, and IFN-I autoantibodies. Bottom right: tissue repair via the Mo-Mac/OSM/p-STAT3 pathway promoting alveolar regeneration. Arrows indicate causal or temporal relationships.Infographic outlining influenza virus pathogenesis with labeled diagrams. Sections explain viral entry and replication, host immune responses including activation and evasion, immunopathology in severe influenza and aging, and tissue repair involving lung macrophages and stem cells. Central illustration shows the influenza virus structure.2.1.Viral determinants of replication, mammalian adaptation, and entryFor avian influenza viruses, one of the first obstacles to productive infection in mammals is receptor use. Avian viruses preferentially recognize α2,3-linked sialic acids, whereas efficient infection of the human upper respiratory tract generally requires greater compatibility with α2,6-linked receptors (Thompson and Paulson, 2021). Receptor preference alone is not sufficient, however. Once entry is possible, the viral polymerase must also function efficiently in mammalian cells.Efficient replication in mammalian cells also depends on polymerase compatibility. Adaptive changes in polymerase proteins, particularly PB2, can increase polymerase activity, replication efficiency, and viral fitness in mammalian hosts (Gilbertson et al., 2023). PB2-E627K and PB2-D701N are well-characterized mammalian-adaptive substitutions, with effects that vary by viral genetic background and host species (Peacock et al., 2023). Human ANP32B promotes the transition of avian-origin H5N1 polymerase from transcriptase to replicase activity by supporting formation of an asymmetric polymerase dimer, thereby facilitating genome replication in mammalian cells (Staller et al., 2024).Non-structural protein 1 (NS1) suppresses antiviral signaling at several levels, including interferon induction and interferon-stimulated gene responses (Zhang et al., 2024). Variation in NS1 function can alter immune evasion, replication fitness, and host adaptation (Evseev and Magor, 2021).PB1-F2, an accessory protein encoded by the PB1 segment, affects mitochondrial function and inflammatory signaling and has been linked to influenza virulence (Cheung et al., 2024). In some settings, it may also increase susceptibility to secondary bacterial infection (Mikušová et al., 2022). The magnitude and direction of these effects vary across viral strains and host backgrounds, so PB1-F2 is better treated as a context-dependent determinant than as a universal marker of pathogenicity.Matrix protein 1 (M1) contributes to uncoating, viral ribonucleoprotein (vRNP) nuclear export, virion assembly, and regulation of polymerase activity. Its conservation and functional importance have made M1 an attractive broad-spectrum antiviral target, although M1-directed approaches remain largely preclinical (Zhu et al., 2025).NS2 forms a domain-swapped dimer and organizes influenza A virus polymerase dimers into a barrel-shaped hexamer. This arrangement restricts interaction between viral polymerase and the C-terminal domain of host RNA polymerase II, favoring a replicase rather than a transcriptase state (Sun et al., 2024). The structure provides a mechanistic explanation for polymerase-state switching; antiviral application remains preclinical.Febrile temperature can alter viral RNA synthesis. By disturbing the balance between viral nucleoprotein and polymerase expression, fever promotes production of aberrant viral RNAs, including mini viral RNAs (mvRNAs). These RNAs activate retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) signaling and can amplify innate immune responses (Bisht et al., 2026). Neuraminidase inhibition reduced lateral viral movement, whereas changes in cell-surface sialic acid density altered diffusion behavior (Yoshida et al., 2025). Most of these mechanisms have not been validated as clinical targets in human influenza.During influenza infection, arrestin domain-containing protein 4 (ARRDC4) is upregulated and increases phosphofructokinase activity, raising fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (FBP) production. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractSeasonal epidemics, zoonotic spillover, antiviral resistance, and pandemic risk continue to make influenza a major challenge for respiratory preparedness. The recent spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in mammalian hosts has made it increasingly important to consider molecular adaptation, surveillance, treatment, and vaccination as connected parts of preparedness rather than as separate issues. This review focuses on four interconnected areas: host–virus interactions, surveillance technologies, antiviral management and resistance, and vaccine preparedness. Evidence on mammalian adaptation includes receptor specificity, viral polymerase–host factor compatibility, innate immune antagonism, ANP32 proteins, and aberrant viral RNA generation, while surveillance has expanded to multiplex and CRISPR-based assays, point-of-care platforms, genomic sequencing, artificial intelligence-assisted risk assessment, and environmental monitoring. These approaches differ in intended use and stage of validation. Antiviral benefit depends strongly on host risk and treatment timing. Resistance-associated substitutions, however, cannot be interpreted from sequence data alone and require phenotypic and epidemiological context. Vaccine development spans nanoparticle, mRNA, and intranasal platforms designed to broaden antigenic coverage, strengthen mucosal immunity, or improve protection in specific populations. Better analytical performance and stronger immune responses do not by themselves demonstrate reductions in severe disease, hospitalization, or mortality. Influenza preparedness ultimately depends on how effectively these four domains inform one another and how consistently emerging approaches are evaluated against clinically meaningful outcomes.Keywords: antiviral resistance, emerging respiratory threats, host–virus interactions, influenza virus, surveillance technologies, vaccine preparedness Graphical abstract The central figure represents the host/patient. The surrounding modules summarize viral threats, pathogenic mechanisms, diagnostic and surveillance approaches, epidemiology and risk stratification, clinical management and recovery, and vaccine development. Examples shown include H5N1 threats; M1, NS2, mvRNA, and RIG-I-related mechanisms; multiplex PCR and CRISPR-based diagnostics; AI-assisted and wastewater surveillance; smartwatch-based recovery assessment; and COBRA, nanoparticle, and mRNA vaccine platforms. The converging arrows indicate the translational focus of the review: using information from these domains to improve protection of human health.Conceptual diagram illustrating host-virus interaction at the center, surrounded by six labeled sections: vaccine development, viral threats, mechanisms and immunity, diagnostics and technologies, epidemiology and surveillance, and treatment, each with icons and relevant keywords summarizing advancements, challenges, and monitoring strategies in influenza research.
full_text_sections.discussion: 7.DiscussionThe evidence reviewed here points to a series of translational handoffs across the four domains. Molecular findings need confirmation in human-derived systems, and surveillance signals need enough standardization to support action. Antiviral susceptibility data require phenotypic and treatment context. Vaccine-induced immune responses must ultimately be assessed against clinically meaningful outcomes. Weakness at any transition can reduce the preparedness value of an otherwise promising approach.Mammalian adaptation shows the distance between mechanistic insight and practical risk assessment. Receptor usage, viral polymerase regulation, ANP32-family proteins, NS1/NS2 function, and aberrant viral RNA generation have refined current models of cross-species adaptation. Much of the evidence still derives from structural studies, cultured cells, or animal models. Human infection adds variables such as age, pre-existing immunity, immunosenescence, fever, and other physiological conditions that can alter viral replication and host responses. Molecular adaptation markers remain candidate risk indicators until supported by human-derived experimental systems, clinical cohorts, and epidemiological evidence.Surveillance signals vary in scale, source, and validation endpoint. Multiplex assays, CRISPR-based platforms, genomic sequencing, AI-assisted analysis, and wastewater monitoring cannot be judged by a single criterion. Sampling procedures, analytical thresholds, and reporting practices add further variation. Wastewater detection of A(H5N1) is especially difficult to interpret because viral material may reflect human shedding, infected animals, or animal waste. Environmental findings are most informative when combined with clinical testing, genomic characterization, epidemiological investigation, and veterinary surveillance within a One Health framework.Clinical management has a similar interpretive constraint. A resistance-associated sequence change is not synonymous with clinical resistance. Phenotypic susceptibility, antiviral exposure, viral subtype, fitness, and treatment outcome remain necessary for judging its significance. Host-directed and TCM-derived interventions are harder to compare because study design, intervention standardization, and quality control vary. Wearable monitoring may capture longitudinal recovery patterns, but useful clinical thresholds and incremental benefit over routine assessment have not been established. These adjunctive and monitoring approaches remain investigational.Vaccine studies make the gap between immune readouts and clinical benefit especially clear. COBRA antigens, nanoparticle vaccines, mRNA platforms, and intranasal approaches address antigenic mismatch, manufacturing speed, or weak mucosal immunity. Broader antibody responses or higher neutralizing titers do not necessarily mean fewer hospitalizations or less severe disease. In older or immunocompromised populations, immunosenescence and impaired cellular immunity can weaken the relationship between serological responses and protection. Evaluation should include humoral, cellular, and mucosal responses, durability, and clinically meaningful outcomes in the intended population.Influenza preparedness depends on how these links function in practice. Evidence of viral adaptation can inform surveillance and risk assessment, and surveillance can guide clinical and public-health responses. Antiviral use generates information relevant to resistance monitoring. Viral evolution and changing population immunity influence vaccine development and updating. Standardized validation, transparent evidence grading, interoperable data sharing, and evaluation in high-risk populations are needed throughout the pathway. During seasonal epidemics, zoonotic outbreaks, or pandemics, the reliability of these links may matter more than the performance of any single technology.
full_text_sections.other: 1.IntroductionThe Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 analysis estimated 2.50 million (95% uncertainty interval [UI], 2.24–2.81 million) lower respiratory infection (LRI) deaths worldwide in 2023 and approximately 22.5 million (19.6–26.5 million) LRI episodes attributable to influenza (GBD 2023 Lower Respiratory Infections and Antimicrobial Resistance Collaborators, 2026). Seasonal influenza remains a substantial component of the global respiratory-disease burden. At the same time, changes in influenza ecology, host range, and the circulation of other respiratory viruses have increased the importance of preparedness for zoonotic as well as seasonal threats.Recent A(H5N1) activity provides a concrete example. Between March 2024 and May 2025, 70 human A(H5N1) infections were reported in the United States, mostly after exposure to infected dairy cattle or poultry; one fatal infection was linked to backyard poultry exposure (Rolfes et al., 2025). Infection of cats with highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in South Korea provides additional evidence of the expanding mammalian host range (Kang et al., 2024). Continued circulation in mammals creates opportunities for further adaptation, so assessment of emerging influenza risk requires molecular information to be interpreted alongside One Health surveillance, clinical risk, antiviral preparedness, and vaccine development.The difficulty is not a lack of recent advances in influenza virology, diagnostics, treatment, resistance surveillance, or vaccination, but the gap between performance in one domain and useful outcomes in another. Findings from cell or animal models may not predict human transmissibility or severity. Low analytical detection limits do not establish clinical utility, sequence-detected resistance markers do not by themselves establish clinically meaningful resistance, and stronger vaccine immunogenicity does not guarantee fewer severe outcomes. These limits are especially important when evidence is applied to older adults, immunocompromised patients, or populations exposed to emerging zoonotic viruses.The review therefore follows four linked dimensions of influenza preparedness: (1) viral and host determinants of replication, mammalian adaptation, and immune responses; (2) multi-layer surveillance for early detection and risk assessment; (3) antiviral treatment, stewardship, and resistance monitoring; and (4) vaccine strategies for broad, durable, and population-specific protection. Epidemiological risk groups, clinical outcomes, and emerging technologies are included only when they inform at least one of these domains. They are not treated as additional pillars. This structure links mechanistic evidence with surveillance, therapeutic decisions, resistance monitoring, and vaccine preparedness in a single narrative.1.1.Literature search strategyPubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for influenza studies published mainly from 2021 through 2026. Initial mapping used the broad concept “influenza,” followed by title-and-abstract screening. The narrative synthesis was limited to four preparedness-oriented domains: host–virus interactions, surveillance and diagnostic technologies, antiviral treatment and resistance, and vaccine preparedness. Earlier publications were retained when they provided essential mechanistic or clinical context. Priority was given to original research, clinical studies, large observational cohorts, surveillance reports, and publications from major public-health organizations. 1.1.Literature search strategyPubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for influenza studies published mainly from 2021 through 2026. Earlier publications were retained when they provided essential mechanistic or clinical context. Recent studies have revealed key mechanisms regulating viral replication, host immunity, and tissue repair (Figure 1).Figure 1Schematic of influenza A virus pathogenesis, host immunity, immunopathology, and tissue repair. The diagram is divided into four quadrants around the virus. Top left: viral entry (lateral diffusion, clathrin recruitment, membrane protrusion, endocytosis) and replication regulation (M1, NS2, ANP32B, fever-induced mvRNA/RIG-I). Top right: host immune responses, including innate activation (ARRDC4/FBP/NF-κB, HSPA1L/NA ubiquitination, neutrophil NET/ROS) and nasal immune quiescence (IRF3↓, low IFN, reversible by exogenous IFN). Bottom left: immunopathology, including severe influenza-associated immune alterations (reduced MAIT-cell responses, increased NK-cell activity, and altered memory B/T-cell responses), aging-related CD8+ T-cell defects, the aged lung PDLIM2/NF-κB axis, and IFN-I autoantibodies. Bottom right: tissue repair via the Mo-Mac/OSM/p-STAT3 pathway promoting alveolar regeneration. Arrows indicate causal or temporal relationships.Infographic outlining influenza virus pathogenesis with labeled diagrams. Sections explain viral entry and replication, host immune responses including activation and evasion, immunopathology in severe influenza and aging, and tissue repair involving lung macrophages and stem cells. Central illustration shows the influenza virus structure.2.1.Viral determinants of replication, mammalian adaptation, and entryFor avian influenza viruses, one of the first obstacles to productive infection in mammals is receptor use. Avian viruses preferentially recognize α2,3-linked sialic acids, whereas efficient infection of the human upper respiratory tract generally requires greater compatibility with α2,6-linked receptors (Thompson and Paulson, 2021). Receptor preference alone is not sufficient, however. Once entry is possible, the viral polymerase must also function efficiently in mammalian cells.Efficient replication in mammalian cells also depends on polymerase compatibility. Adaptive changes in polymerase proteins, particularly PB2, can increase polymerase activity, replication efficiency, and viral fitness in mammalian hosts (Gilbertson et al., 2023). PB2-E627K and PB2-D701N are well-characterized mammalian-adaptive substitutions, with effects that vary by viral genetic background and host species (Peacock et al., 2023). analysis.research_question_and_background: This review addresses the need to integrate molecular adaptation, surveillance, treatment, and vaccination strategies to enhance preparedness against seasonal influenza and emerging respiratory threats.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a comprehensive review of evidence from multiple domains, including host–virus interactions, surveillance technologies, antiviral management, and vaccine development, focusing on human influenza and its ecological and epidemiological contexts.
analysis.methods: The review synthesizes evidence on mammalian adaptation, such as receptor specificity and viral polymerase–host factor compatibility, alongside surveillance technologies like multiplex PCR, CRISPR-based assays, and AI-assisted risk assessment, and evaluates antiviral management and vaccine platforms including nanoparticle, mRNA, and intranasal designs.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights that recent A(H5N1) infections in humans, particularly in the United States, have been linked to exposure to infected dairy cattle or poultry, with one fatal case associated with backyard poultry exposure. It also notes the expanding mammalian host range of A(H5N1) as evidenced by its infection of cats in South Korea.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the integration of findings across the four domains is critical for improving influenza preparedness, and that current evidence often relies on structural studies, cultured cells, or animal models, which may not fully capture human infection complexities.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for standardized surveillance systems and better understanding of antiviral resistance and vaccine efficacy in relation to clinically meaningful outcomes, particularly for emerging threats like A(H5N1) in human populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is primarily derived from non-human models and structural studies, which may limit its direct applicability to human health. The review identifies weaknesses in translational handoffs between domains, suggesting moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses the need to integrate molecular adaptation, surveillance, treatment, and vaccination strategies to enhance preparedness against seasonal influenza and emerging respiratory threats. It evaluates evidence on mammalian adaptation, surveillance technologies, and vaccine platforms, highlighting recent A(H5N1) infections in humans and the expanding host range of the virus. The authors emphasize the importance of connecting findings across domains to improve human health protection, noting that current evidence often relies on non-human models and structural studies. The review identifies limitations in the translational focus and the need for standardized surveillance and phenotypic context for antiviral resistance. These findings suggest that while the evidence is informative, its application to human health remains constrained by the reliance on animal models and the lack of direct clinical validation, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本综述解决了整合分子适应、监测、治疗 和 疫苗接种 策略的需要,以加强针对 季节性流感 和新出现的呼吸道威胁的准备。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对来自多个领域的证据进行了全面审查,包括 宿主 与病毒相互作用、监测 技术、抗病毒药物 管理和 疫苗 开发,重点关注人类流感及其生态和流行病学背景。
analysis_zh.methods: 该综述综合了哺乳动物适应的证据,例如受体特异性和病毒聚合酶-宿主因子兼容性,以及多重PCR、基于CRISPR的检测和人工智能辅助风险评估等监测技术,并评估了抗病毒药物管理和疫苗平台,包括纳米颗粒、mRNA和鼻内设计。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该审查强调,最近发生的人类 A(H5N1) 感染,特别是在美国,与接触受感染的奶牛或家禽有关,其中一例死亡病例与接触后院家禽有关。它还注意到 A(H5N1) 哺乳动物 宿主 范围的扩大,韩国猫的感染就证明了这一点。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,整合四个领域的研究结果对于改善流感防范至关重要,目前的证据通常依赖于结构研究、培养细胞或动物模型,而这些可能无法完全捕捉人类感染的复杂性。

papers.title: The antigenic landscape of N1 neuraminidase in human influenza A virus strains isolated between 2009 and 2020
papers.abstract: The immunogen composition of seasonal influenza vaccines is revised biannually to match the antigenic drift of the hemagglutinin of circulating influenza virus strains. Antibodies directed against the influenza neuraminidase also correlate with protection against influenza, yet the antigenic evolution of influenza neuraminidase remains underexplored. To evaluate the antigenic diversity of N1 neuraminidase, we generated a panel of immune sera in mice directed against 17 N1 neuraminidases derived from human H1N1 strains that were isolated between 2009 and 2020 and determined the neuraminidase inhibition (NAI) titers of these sera against a panel of 14 HxN1 viruses. The selected N1 neuraminidases cluster into two major phylogenetic groups while the NAI pattern revealed two antigenic groups corresponding to early and more recent H1N1 viruses. Sera raised against early N1 NAs inhibited NA activity from both early and recent H1N1 viruses equally well, whereas sera raised against more recent N1 NAs showed stronger NAI against recent H1N1 strains, indicating an asymmetric antigenic relationship between the two antigenic groups. Random forest modeling of antigenic distances indicated that the I321V, N386K/S and K432E substitutions played an important role in the N1 NA antigenic variation. Reverse-genetics experiments using mutant strains revealed that the N386K substitution in an early H1N1 virus increased susceptibility to inhibition by sera raised against recent N1 NAs, consistent with a role for the loss of the N-linked glycosylation motif and the acquisition of a lysine at this position near the lateral surface of the NA head. However, reciprocal substitutions in a recent N1 background did not restore the early antigenic phenotype, indicating a unidirectional effect. This finding suggests that anti-NA responses elicited against early pandemic H1N1 viruses remained effective against circulating N1 variants up to at least 2020.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决尚未开发的流感神经氨酸酶抗原 进化,这对于 疫苗 的开发至关重要,因为 季节性流感 疫苗 的免疫原组成每半年修订一次,以匹配循环流感病毒株血凝素的 抗原漂移。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及在小鼠中生成一组针对源自 2009 年至 2020 年间分离的人类 H1N1 病毒株的 17 种 N1 神经氨酸酶的免疫血清,并确定这些血清针对一组 14 种 HxN1 病毒的神经氨酸酶抑制 (NAI) 滴度。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用反向遗传学实验来评估特定取代在 N1 神经氨酸酶抗原变异中的作用,并应用随机森林模型来分析基于 NAI 滴度的抗原距离。
elements_zh.main_results: 所选的 N1 神经氨酸酶聚类为两个主要的系统发育群,NAI 模式揭示了与早期和较近期的 H1N1 病毒相对应的两个抗原组。针对早期 N1 NA 的血清对早期和近期 H1N1 病毒的 NA 活性具有同样的抑制作用,而针对较近期 N1 NA 的血清对近期 H1N1 病毒株表现出更强的 NAI。反向遗传学实验表明,早期 H1N1 病毒中的 N386K 取代增加了对近期 N1 NA 血清抑制的敏感性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,两组之间存在不对称抗原关系,针对早期大流行 H1N1 病毒的抗 NA 反应至少到 2020 年仍然对循环的 N1 变种有效。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,N1 神经氨酸酶的抗原性 进化 可能会影响抗 NA 反应的有效性,这可以为 疫苗 设计和 季节性流感 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到小鼠模型的使用以及 免疫应答 中物种特异性差异的可能性的限制,但由于对抗原距离的详细分析和替代的实验验证,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Self-Assembling Nanoparticles to Assess Multivalent Interactions between Influenza A Virus Hemagglutinin and Glycan Surfaces
papers.abstract: The multivalent display of surface glycoprotein hemagglutinin (HA) on Influenza A viruses (IAVs) enhances the overall binding avidity to sialylated glycans on host cell surfaces. While precomplexing HA trimers with antibodies increases multivalency and avidity, this method does not replicate the virion's geometry and limits insights into the multivalent binding process. Here, we use perfectly controllable icosahedral protein nanoparticles to examine the multivalent HA receptor-binding properties. We compare three HA presentation systems with varying degrees of multivalency: single HA trimers, antibody-precomplexed HA trimers, and HA trimers on nanoparticles. Our results indicate that increasing HA valency enhances binding avidity across various glycan surfaces, including erythrocytes, cells, and lipid bilayers with varying glycan densities, while maintaining receptor specificity. By combining functional and nonfunctional HA trimers during nanoparticle formation, we create statistical mixtures of nanoparticles with varying valencies. At high receptor densities, nanoparticles with few functional trimers still bind strongly, whereas at low receptor densities, a patch of five HA trimers appears necessary for binding. As a key finding, we observe that such a statistical mixture of nanoparticles with functional and nonfunctional HAs binds to glycan surfaces in a stronger density-dependent manner than fully functional particles. We also observe differences in binding modes that correlate with the number of functional trimers, the glycan structure (linear vs branched), and the densities achievable with these glycans. Overall, our findings demonstrate that the presentation of multivalent HA plays an enormous role in the response to glycan receptor type and density, with implications for the future design of virus monitoring, viral inhibitors, and targeting vectors.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用完全可控的二十面体蛋白纳米颗粒来检查多价 HA 受体结合特性,比较了三种 HA 呈递系统:单一 HA 三聚体、抗体预复合的 HA 三聚体和纳米颗粒上的 HA 三聚体。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过在纳米颗粒形成过程中结合功能性和非功能性 HA 三聚体,创建了具有不同化合价的纳米颗粒的统计混合物,并评估了它们与不同结构和密度的聚糖表面的结合。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,增加 HA 价数可增强跨各种聚糖表面(包括红细胞、细胞和脂质双层)的结合亲合力,同时保持受体特异性。在高受体密度下,具有少量功能性三聚体的纳米颗粒仍然牢固结合,而在低受体密度下,五个 HA 三聚体的补丁似乎需要结合。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HA 的多价呈现显着影响对聚糖受体类型和密度的反应,为 HA 结合如何通过价态调节提供了新的见解。

papers.abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 上表面糖蛋白血凝素 (HA) 的多价展示增强了 宿主 细胞表面唾液酸化聚糖的整体结合亲和力。虽然 HA 三聚体与抗体预复合可增加多价性和亲合力,但该方法无法复制病毒粒子的几何形状,并限制了对多价结合过程的了解。在这里,我们使用完全可控的二十面体蛋白质纳米粒子来检查多价 HA 受体结合特性。我们比较了三种具有不同多价程度的HA呈现系统:单一HA三聚体、抗体预复合HA三聚体和纳米颗粒上的HA三聚体。我们的结果表明,增加HA价数可以增强跨各种聚糖表面的结合亲和力,包括红细胞、细胞和具有不同聚糖密度的脂质双层,同时保持受体特异性。通过在纳米颗粒形成过程中结合功能性和非功能性 HA 三聚体,我们创建了具有不同化合价的纳米颗粒的统计混合物。在高受体密度下,具有少量功能性三聚体的纳米颗粒仍然牢固结合,而在低受体密度下,五个 HA 三聚体的补丁似乎需要结合。作为一项重要发现,我们观察到,这种具有功能性和非功能性 HA 的纳米颗粒的统计混合物比全功能颗粒以更强的密度依赖性方式与聚糖表面结合。我们还观察到与功能三聚体数量、聚糖结构(线性与支链)以及这些聚糖可实现的密度相关的结合模式的差异。总体而言,我们的研究结果表明,多价 HA 的呈现在聚糖受体类型和密度的反应中发挥着巨大作用,对病毒监测、病毒抑制剂和靶向 媒介 的未来设计具有影响。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 上血凝素 (HA) 的多价展示如何影响 宿主 细胞表面唾液酸化聚糖的结合亲和力,从而弥补有关 HA 价在病毒相互作用中的作用的知识空白。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用完全可控的二十面体蛋白纳米颗粒来检查多价 HA 受体结合特性,比较了三种 HA 呈递系统:单一 HA 三聚体、抗体预复合的 HA 三聚体和纳米颗粒上的 HA 三聚体。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员通过在纳米颗粒形成过程中结合功能性和非功能性 HA 三聚体,创建了具有不同化合价的纳米颗粒的统计混合物,并评估了它们与不同结构和密度的聚糖表面的结合。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,增加 HA 价数可增强跨各种聚糖表面(包括红细胞、细胞和脂质双层)的结合亲合力,同时保持受体特异性。在高受体密度下,具有少量功能性三聚体的纳米颗粒仍然牢固结合,而在低受体密度下,五个 HA 三聚体的补丁似乎需要结合。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HA 的多价呈现显着影响对聚糖受体类型和密度的反应,为 HA 结合如何通过价态调节提供了新的见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对病毒监测、病毒抑制剂和靶向 媒介 的未来设计具有影响,可能为改进 疫苗 和 抗病毒药物 开发的策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据是强有力的,因为它使用受控实验系统来检查HA价效应,但它没有考虑体内条件或自然病毒变异,这可能会限制普遍性。
