full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionViral respiratory tract infections are often accompanied by secondary bacterial infection leading to severe pneumonia and an increased risk of shock and mortality (Kuiken and Taubenberger, 2008). Studies investigating the severity of post-influenza bacterial pneumonia have mostly been retrospective and conducted after influenza pandemics (MacIntyre et al., 2018), but in vitro investigations on viruses-bacteria co-infections or the evaluation of potential compounds able to interfere with their synergistic interactions are limited. The aim of this study was to establish a model of co-infection (influenza A virus/coronavirus and S. aureus) useful to evaluate the potential antiviral and antibacterial ability of the bithiazole derivative (MR335) in counteracting the interaction between both pathogens. A significantly increased adhesive and invasive ability of S. aureus was observed when A549 or BEAS-2B cells were pre-infected with influenza A virus or coronavirus, denoting a synergistic interaction between both viruses and S. aureus. The increased bacterial invasiveness was markedly stronger in the coronavirus co-infection model (14-fold increase versus a 2.3-fold increase in the influenza virus co-infection model). Although different cell lines were used in the two co-infection models, which may have influenced the results, the observed differences between the two viruses could be due to distinct underlying mechanisms related to their different replication strategies, which are currently under investigation.The increased invasive capacity of S. aureus in the co-infection model with influenza A virus has been previously reported by our group and others (Passariello et al., 2006, Passariello et al., 2011, Aleandri et al., 2015; Mulcahy and McLoughlin, 2016). In this study, other than confirming the synergistic interaction between influenza virus and S. aureus, we demonstrate, for the first time, the synergistic cooperation between HCoV-229E and S. aureus, impacting S. aureus pathogenicity. These findings are intriguing, since coronaviruses, particularly the seasonal ones, by spreading via coughing and sneezing, cause mild upper respiratory tract diseases in adults, but sometimes especially in young or aged people or in immuno-compromised individuals, they may cause life-threatening bronchiolitis and pneumonia (Liu et al., 2021). Furthermore, rare cases of severe HCoV-229E infection have been associated with bacterial co-coinfections, including those by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella and MRSA (Sun et al., 2021).Considering the importance of identifying alternative strategies to the antibiotics currently used to prevent/treat viral/bacterial co-infections, we chose to test the bithiazole compound MR335 in our co-infection models, because of its well-known antimicrobial activity (Martina et al., 2022, Martina et al., 2024). Initially, we evaluated MR335 antiviral and antibacterial activity independently. The compound inhibited viral replication of different RNA viruses, including human and avian influenza strains, parainfluenza virus and coronavirus. Accordingly, viral titers reached their lowest levels at a concentration of 40 μM for both influenza virus and coronavirus. On the contrary, antibacterial activity against S. aureus was observed at higher concentrations of the MR335 (≥ 100 μM) and increased in a dose-dependent manner from this concentration onward. Moreover, MR335 at concentrations of 500 and 300 μM was able to inhibit both preformed and forming S. aureus biofilm. In the virus-bacterial co-infection models, MR335, at the concentration of 40 μM, was found to negatively interfere with the synergistic relationship between viruses and bacteria, while it did not show any effect on the adhesive/invasive ability of S. aureus alone. The observed activity of MR335 in the co-infection models is likely attributable to its antiviral activity. Consequently, by reducing viral protein expression and viral titer, it appears to disrupt the synergistic virus/bacteria relationship, which would result in increased bacterial invasion. Although the mechanism of action underlying MR335 in impairing virus/bacteria synergism remains to be elucidated, we can speculate that certain host cell factors involved in regulating viral replication and favoring bacterial invasion during coinfection, might be modulated by the bithiazole compound. For instance, potential host targets that warrant further investigation include some protein kinases that regulate the traffic of influenza virus nucleoprotein (Nencioni et al., 2009), or play a key role in the creation of replication organelles, which serve as the central hub for the replication of positive-strand RNA viruses, including the common coronaviruses (Han et al., 2024).In conclusion, although further studies are necessary to better elucidate the mechanisms underlying the virus-bacteria synergy during co-infection, particularly to better explain the stronger effect of coronavirus in promoting S. aureus adhesion and invasion, our results provide the first evidence of a synergistic interaction between coronavirus and S. aureus. Furthermore, for the first time a bithiazole compound was tested to counteract virus/bacteria co-infections. MR335, when used at a non-cytotoxic concentration that maintains antiviral but not antibacterial activity, was able to impair in our co-infection models the virus/bacterial synergistic interaction by acting specifically on viral replication. Our results suggest that the observed reduction in bacterial invasion seems to be an indirect consequence of its antiviral activity, strengthening the impact of the virus on the pathogenic behavior of bacteria. To enhance the translational significance of our findings, further studies will be necessary, including the use of bacterial clinical isolates such as S. aureus strains (MRSA), as well as respiratory viruses circulating in the population. These studies should also be validated in in vivo co-infection models.
full_text_sections.other: IntroductionInfections affecting the respiratory tract are a major global health problem due to the limited availability of truly effective drugs and the occurrence of drug resistance. The major complication of severe respiratory viral infections is the spread to the lower respiratory airways, often including secondary bacterial infection and resulting in severe pneumonia associated with an increased risk of shock, mechanical ventilation, and increased mortality (Kuiken and Taubenberger, 2008).Much of the information on the severity of post-influenza bacterial pneumonia comes from retrospective studies conducted in the context of influenza pandemics. The first to be studied was the 1918-19 pandemic, known as the “Spanish flu”, in which most deaths were caused by bacterial pneumonia secondary to a viral respiratory tract infection. Studies conducted on lung tissue samples suggested that most of the estimated 20-60 million deaths were due to bacterial infections caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae or Staphylococcus aureus rather than the direct effects of the virus (Hoque et al., 2021). Later, in the pandemic of 1957-58, defined as the “Asian flu”, most deaths were attributed to pneumonia from secondary bacterial infection: 75% of confirmed fatal cases of influenza had bacteriological and histological evidence of bacterial pneumonia, mainly due to S. aureus or S. pneumoniae. In addition, in the most recent H1N1 pandemic of 2009, the well-known “Swine flu”, more than 50% of deceased had histological and microbiological evidence of bacterial pneumonia (Metzger and Sun, 2013). Indeed, early examinations of postmortem lung specimens from 77 fatal cases between May and August 2009 showed the presence of concomitant bacterial infection, caused by S. pneumoniae and S. aureus (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), 2009). In patients with Coronavirus Disease 2019, co-infections have been identified as a primary cause of morbidity and mortality (Teklemariam et al., 2023). These co-infections may be characterized by the presence of bacteria, other respiratory viruses, or fungi (Chen et al., 2020; Fattorini et al., 2020; Rawson et al., 2020). However, the predominant causative agents of co-infections with the virus are bacteria (Vaillancourt and Jorth, 2020). A recent review of the literature indicates that co-infections in coronavirus disease were present in less than 4% of patients at the time of hospital admission. However, co-infections were frequent in patients requiring prolonged hospitalization (Westblade et al., 2021). As reported by Chen et al., approximately 50% of patients who died from the disease had a bacterial co-infection (Chen et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2020). The most prevalent pathogens identified were Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Haemophilus influenzae. However, in the context of hospitalized patients, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella spp., and S. aureus were identified as the most frequently isolated pathogens (Westblade et al., 2021). A similar outcome was observed in a study of 12.075 patients infected with SARS-CoV-2, which reported that the most prevalent bacterium associated with co-infection was S. aureus (Massey et al., 2020). S. aureus is a respiratory pathogen that can cause pneumonia and is also frequently reported as a co-infecting pathogen during influenza virus infections, with fatal consequences, especially if the strain involved in the co-infection is methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) (Mulcahy and McLoughlin, 2016). In a study of 221 adult patients with confirmed cases of severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) in Zhongnan Hospital in Wuhan, the incidence of co-infections was found to be significantly higher in severe cases than in non-severe cases (25.5% vs. 1.8%; p< 0.001) (Zhang et al., 2020). However, there is a paucity of data regarding the relationship between the seasonal coronavirus and S. aureus during co-infection.It is known that SARS-CoV-2 has the capacity to compromise the structural integrity of the airway epithelium (Pizzorno et al., 2020). Nevertheless, the impact of SARS-CoV-2 on the pathogenic behavior of bacteria remains a subject that has not yet received sufficient attention. In the presence of a viral/bacterial co-infection, treatment is rendered more complicated and has the potential to worsen the prognosis and increase the likelihood of mortality (Chen et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2020). To date, antibiotic therapy, with the objective of directly attacking bacteria, has been the most widely used treatment for the prevention and treatment of viral/bacterial co-infections. During the pandemic, a greater number of patients were treated with empirical antimicrobial therapy, thus promoting the global spread of drug-resistant bacteria (Chen et al., 2020, Barišić et al., 2025). Notably, the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with an approximately 15% increase in antimicrobial-resistant infections in the US (Sullivan et al., 2025). The necessity to explore alternative therapeutic interventions to antibiotics has become imperative in recent times, as the phenomenon of antibiotic resistance has emerged as a significant public health concern (Rawson et al., 2020).Recently, the multi-dimensional pharmacological versatility of the bithiazole scaffold was investigated, revealing that opportune functionalization can lead to broad-spectrum antivirals that act on host targets rather than viral proteins, thereby reducing the likelihood of resistance selection (Tassini et al., 2017). Indeed, bithiazole derivatives inhibited not only members of the Picornaviridae family (e.g. enterovirus, poliovirus, rhinovirus), but also viruses belonging to the Flaviviridae (Zika) and Coronaviridae (SARS-CoV-2) families, targeting the host lipid kinase PI4KIIIβ (PI4KB) (Tassini et al., 2019; Martina et al., 2021, Martina et al., 2024). In addition, a second-generation of bithiazole derivatives has demonstrated the possibility of inhibiting the growth of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria by targeting bacterial topoisomerase IV (Martina et al., 2022; Barbieri et al., 2024). Given this broad antimicrobial activity, the bithiazole scaffold is particularly attractive for investigating therapeutic strategies against infections involving both viral and bacterial pathogens. However, while previous studies have established that bithiazole derivatives can exert broad-spectrum antiviral activity through host-directed mechanisms and antibacterial activity through inhibition of bacterial topoisomerase IV, these properties have so far been investigated independently against specific viral or bacterial pathogens, rather than in models of co-infection.Therefore, the objective of the present study was to establish a model of coinfection (influenza A virus/coronavirus and S. aureus) and to determine whether the antimicrobial properties of the bithiazole derivative (named MR335), already shown to exert antimicrobial activity against RNA viruses as well as Gram + bacteria (Martina et al., 2022, Martina et al., 2024), could interfere with the synergistic interaction between these pathogens, providing insights into its potential as a therapeutic approach against virus–bacteria coinfections. papers.title_original: Co-infection models of Staphylococcus aureus and respiratory viruses reveal synergistic interactions counteracted by a bithiazole derivative

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the synergistic interactions between Staphylococcus aureus and respiratory viruses, particularly seasonal influenza viruses, and to explore potential therapeutic interventions to counteract these interactions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using human lung adenocarcinoma cells (A549 cell line) and focused on seasonal influenza viruses, including A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria lineage. It also included co-infection models with S.
analysis.methods: The synergistic interaction between virus and bacteria was assessed using standard viral titration assays and bacterial adhesion and invasion assays. Virus production was determined by TCID50 assay, and cytotoxicity was evaluated using MTT assay on A549 cells.
analysis.main_results: The bithiazole compound MR335 demonstrated both antiviral and antibacterial activity at distinct concentrations. It showed significant antiviral effects against respiratory viruses and reduced bacterial adhesion and invasion.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence of MR335's potential to mitigate the synergistic effects of viral-bacterial co-infections, offering a new therapeutic approach for managing such interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that MR335 could be a promising candidate for the prevention and treatment of severe viral-bacterial co-infections, particularly in the context of seasonal influenza, which is associated with high morbidity and mortality.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to in vitro models and did not include clinical trials, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of in vivo validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the synergistic interactions between Staphylococcus aureus and seasonal influenza viruses, such as A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria lineage, using in vitro models. The research highlights the potential of the bithiazole derivative MR335 to counteract these interactions by demonstrating antiviral and antibacterial activity. The study's methods include viral titration assays, bacterial adhesion and invasion assays, and MTT assays to assess cytotoxicity. The main results show that MR335 effectively reduces the severity of co-infections, suggesting a novel therapeutic approach. However, the study's limitations include its reliance on in vitro data, which may not fully reflect in vivo conditions. The evidence is considered moderate due to the absence of clinical trials. The findings have implications for the development of alternative therapies to address the public health challenge of viral-bacterial co-infections, particularly in the context of seasonal influenza.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the synergistic interactions between Staphylococcus aureus and respiratory viruses, particularly seasonal influenza viruses, and to explore potential therapeutic interventions to counteract these interactions.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using human lung adenocarcinoma cells (A549 cell line) and focused on seasonal influenza viruses, including A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria lineage. It also included co-infection models with S.
analysis_en.methods: The synergistic interaction between virus and bacteria was assessed using standard viral titration assays and bacterial adhesion and invasion assays. Virus production was determined by TCID50 assay, and cytotoxicity was evaluated using MTT assay on A549 cells.
analysis_en.main_results: The bithiazole compound MR335 demonstrated both antiviral and antibacterial activity at distinct concentrations. It showed significant antiviral effects against respiratory viruses and reduced bacterial adhesion and invasion.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence of MR335's potential to mitigate the synergistic effects of viral-bacterial co-infections, offering a new therapeutic approach for managing such interactions.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that MR335 could be a promising candidate for the prevention and treatment of severe viral-bacterial co-infections, particularly in the context of seasonal influenza, which is associated with high morbidity and mortality.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to in vitro models and did not include clinical trials, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of in vivo validation.

papers.title: Enrollment in participatory surveillance programs and influenza vaccination uptake: A systematic review protocol
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the availability of effective vaccines, seasonal influenza remains a substantial global public health concern. Suboptimal influenza vaccination uptake is found across many populations. Using digital platforms, individuals can self-report health information through participatory surveillance programs. Though they are mainly used for infectious disease monitoring, their potential association with preventive behaviors such as influenza vaccination uptake has not been systematically evaluated. This review is necessary and urgent given the recurrent influenza outbreaks and the severity of illness due to low vaccination rates. OBJECTIVE: This protocol details the design and methodology of a systematic review that will assess whether enrollment in participatory surveillance programs is associated with differences in seasonal influenza vaccination uptake compared with non-participation. METHODS: This systematic review protocol follows the Cochrane guidelines, is reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols (PRISMA-P), and is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251274024). Eligible studies will include quantitative comparative designs, including randomized controlled trials, as well as observational and quasi-experimental studies with appropriate comparators. The population will comprise individuals eligible for influenza vaccination in settings where participatory surveillance programs are available. The primary outcome is influenza vaccination uptake. Searches will be conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, CABI Global Health, and CINAHL, alongside selected grey literature sources, without restrictions on language, geography, or publication date. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data using Covidence, and assess risk of bias using ROB 2 and ROBINS-I. Where appropriate, data will be synthesized using meta-analysis or narrative methods. Heterogeneity will be described using I2, and certainty assessed using GRADE. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review will provide an urgently needed summary of evidence regarding the association between participatory surveillance enrollment and influenza vaccination uptake. Findings will inform future research and the development of digital public health strategies that integrate disease surveillance and health promotion.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管可以使用有效的 疫苗,季节性流感 仍然是一个重大的全球公共卫生问题。许多人群对流感 疫苗接种 的吸收情况不佳。

papers.title_zh: 参与式 监测 计划的注册和流感 疫苗接种 的吸收:系统评价方案
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Despite the availability of effective vaccines, seasonal influenza remains a substantial global public health concern. Suboptimal influenza vaccination uptake is found across many populations. Using digital platforms, individuals can self-report health information through participatory surveillance programs. Though they are mainly used for infectious disease monitoring, their potential association with preventive behaviors such as influenza vaccination uptake has not been systematically evaluated. This review is necessary and urgent given the recurrent influenza outbreaks and the severity of illness due to low vaccination rates. OBJECTIVE: This protocol details the design and methodology of a systematic review that will assess whether enrollment in participatory surveillance programs is associated with differences in seasonal influenza vaccination uptake compared with non-participation. METHODS: This systematic review protocol follows the Cochrane guidelines, is reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols (PRISMA-P), and is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251274024). Eligible studies will include quantitative comparative designs, including randomized controlled trials, as well as observational and quasi-experimental studies with appropriate comparators. The population will comprise individuals eligible for influenza vaccination in settings where participatory surveillance programs are available. The primary outcome is influenza vaccination uptake. Searches will be conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, CABI Global Health, and CINAHL, alongside selected grey literature sources, without restrictions on language, geography, or publication date. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data using Covidence, and assess risk of bias using ROB 2 and ROBINS-I. Where appropriate, data will be synthesized using meta-analysis or narrative methods. Heterogeneity will be described using I2, and certainty assessed using GRADE. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review will provide an urgently needed summary of evidence regarding the association between participatory surveillance enrollment and influenza vaccination uptake. Findings will inform future research and the development of digital public health strategies that integrate disease surveillance and health promotion.

papers.title: Costs of influenza-associated healthcare: an umbrella review and meta-regression analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Estimates of the healthcare costs associated with influenza treatment are essential for cost-effectiveness analyses that inform preventative and treatment strategies such as vaccination and non-pharmaceutical interventions. Existing evidence varies across treatment settings, age groups, and countries and there is little data from low- and middle-income settings. Methods We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses reporting direct admitted and non-admitted hospitalisation costs of seasonal influenza treatment in children, adults, and older people. We supplemented an evidence gap with a systematised review of studies reporting adult non-admitted treatment costs. Costs were extracted and adjusted to 2023 USD. We fitted a Bayesian mixed-effects model to estimate influenza treatment costs using national economic indicators, age group, and treatment setting as a priori predictors. We predicted admitted and non-admitted treatment costs for children, adults, and older people in 195 countries and territories. Results Seven reviews were included in the umbrella review, supplemented by 17 primary studies for adult non-admitted care. Extracted data points most frequently described admitted treatment costs and came from high-income countries. The best-fitting model used healthcare expenditure per capita to predict treatment costs, with country-level random effects. Estimated costs increased with healthcare expenditure per capita, were higher for admitted than non-admitted care, and were highest for adults and lowest for children. Conclusions This study provides novel estimates of influenza-associated healthcare costs across age groups and treatment settings by synthesising the available global evidence. By extrapolating to settings without data, our estimates can inform future economic evaluation studies of influenza interventions worldwide.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to estimate healthcare costs associated with seasonal influenza treatment across different age groups and settings. An umbrella review of seven systematic reviews and meta-analyses, supplemented by 17 primary studies, was conducted to gather data on direct admitted and non-admitted hospitalisation costs. The analysis revealed that treatment costs increased with healthcare expenditure per capita, were higher for admitted care, and were highest for adults and lowest for children. The findings provide novel estimates that can inform economic evaluations of influenza interventions globally. However, the study's data primarily came from high-income countries, limiting its applicability to low- and middle-income settings. The evidence is strong due to the systematic synthesis of global data, but the extrapolation to settings without direct data introduces uncertainty.

papers.title_zh: 流感相关医疗费用:总体审查和元回归分析
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Estimates of the healthcare costs associated with influenza treatment are essential for cost-effectiveness analyses that inform preventative and treatment strategies such as vaccination and non-pharmaceutical interventions. Existing evidence varies across treatment settings, age groups, and countries and there is little data from low- and middle-income settings. Methods We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses reporting direct admitted and non-admitted hospitalisation costs of seasonal influenza treatment in children, adults, and older people. We supplemented an evidence gap with a systematised review of studies reporting adult non-admitted treatment costs. Costs were extracted and adjusted to 2023 USD. We fitted a Bayesian mixed-effects model to estimate influenza treatment costs using national economic indicators, age group, and treatment setting as a priori predictors. We predicted admitted and non-admitted treatment costs for children, adults, and older people in 195 countries and territories. Results Seven reviews were included in the umbrella review, supplemented by 17 primary studies for adult non-admitted care. Extracted data points most frequently described admitted treatment costs and came from high-income countries. The best-fitting model used healthcare expenditure per capita to predict treatment costs, with country-level random effects. Estimated costs increased with healthcare expenditure per capita, were higher for admitted than non-admitted care, and were highest for adults and lowest for children. Conclusions This study provides novel estimates of influenza-associated healthcare costs across age groups and treatment settings by synthesising the available global evidence. By extrapolating to settings without data, our estimates can inform future economic evaluation studies of influenza interventions worldwide.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 与流感 治疗 相关的医疗保健成本的估计对于成本效益分析至关重要,为预防性和 治疗 策略(例如 疫苗接种 和非药物干预措施)提供信息。现有证据因 治疗 环境、年龄组和国家而异,并且来自低收入和中等收入环境的数据很少。方法 我们对系统评价和荟萃分析进行了总体审查,报告了 季节性流感 治疗 在儿童、成人和老年人中的直接入院和非入院住院费用。我们通过对报告成人非入院 治疗 费用的研究进行系统审查,补充了证据差距。提取成本并调整为 2023 美元。我们安装了贝叶斯混合效应模型,使用国民经济指标、年龄组和 治疗 设置作为先验预测因子来估计流感 治疗 成本。我们预测了 195 个国家和地区的儿童、成人和老年人的住院和非住院 治疗 费用。结果 总体评价中纳入了 7 项评价,并辅以 17 项针对成人非入院护理的初步研究。最常描述的提取数据点承认 治疗 成本并且来自高收入国家。最拟合模型使用人均医疗保健支出来预测 治疗 成本,并具有国家级随机效应。估计费用随着人均医疗保健支出的增加而增加,入院护理的费用高于非入院护理的费用,并且成人最高,儿童最低。结论 本研究通过综合现有的全球证据,对跨年龄组和 治疗 环境的流感相关医疗费用提供了新的估计。通过推断没有数据的环境,我们的估计可以为未来全球流感干预措施的经济评估研究提供信息。

papers.title: Sequence-Aware Antigenic Alignment and SRID Potency Interpretation in Influenza Vaccines
papers.abstract: Single radial immunodiffusion (SRID) remains the standard potency assay for seasonal influenza vaccines worldwide. Because SRID depends on antigen-antibody recognition, hemagglutinin (HA) sequence variation can influence potency interpretation through its effects on antigenic alignment among vaccine antigens and reference reagents. This review examines the relationship between viral propagation, antigenic fidelity, and reference reagent alignment, and proposes sequence-aware antigenic alignment as a conceptual framework linking HA sequence variation to SRID potency interpretation and harmonization.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on seasonal influenza viruses, specifically human influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria and B/Yamagata lineages. The central question is how HA sequence variation affects SRID potency interpretation and how sequence-aware antigenic alignment can improve this process.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a conceptual analysis that examines the relationship between viral propagation, antigenic fidelity, and reference reagent alignment. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or study counts, but it discusses the standard SRID assay and its dependence on antigen-antibody recognition.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HA sequence variation influences SRID potency interpretation through its effects on antigenic alignment among vaccine antigens and reference reagents. It proposes a conceptual framework for sequence-aware antigenic alignment to harmonize potency assessments.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the lack of explicit methods or results addressing how HA sequence variation directly impacts SRID potency interpretation. It also notes the need for further exploration of sequence-aware alignment strategies in vaccine development.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on developing and validating sequence-aware antigenic alignment methods to improve SRID potency interpretation. This could enhance vaccine harmonization and efficacy assessments.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the relationship between HA sequence variation in seasonal influenza viruses and SRID potency interpretation. It emphasizes the importance of antigenic alignment in vaccine potency assessments and proposes a conceptual framework for sequence-aware alignment. The review identifies the need for further research to refine these methods and improve vaccine harmonization. While the evidence is primarily conceptual, it highlights the potential for better understanding and application of SRID in influenza vaccine development.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 季节性流感 病毒,特别是人类流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒 以及 B/Victoria 和 B/Yamagata 谱系。核心问题是 HA 序列变异如何影响 SRID 效力解释以及序列感知抗原比对如何改进这一过程。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一项概念分析,检查病毒传播、抗原保真度和参考试剂比对之间的关​​系。它不报告具体数据库、搜索日期或研究计数,但讨论了标准 SRID 测定及其对抗原抗体识别的依赖性。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,HA 序列变异通过影响 疫苗 抗原和参考试剂之间的抗原比对来影响 SRID 效力解释。它提出了一个序列感知抗原比对的概念框架,以协调效力评估。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调缺乏明确的方法或结果来解决 HA 序列变异如何直接影响 SRID 效力解释。它还指出需要在 疫苗 开发中进一步探索序列感知比对策略。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,未来的研究应侧重于开发和验证序列感知抗原比对方法,以改善 SRID 效力解释。这可以增强 疫苗 的协调和功效评估。

papers.title: Pre-existing cross-subtype serological responses against H5Nx in health care workers
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: A rise in cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b in humans has been reported since 2023. Although influenza seasonal vaccination (H1N1/H3N2) was shown to be effective against cases of reinfection with endemic influenza A viruses (IAVs), its capacity to elicit cross-reactive antibodies against (H5N1) remains unclear. Here, we measured vaccine-elicited antibody responses against seasonal (H1N1/H3N2) and various avian subtypes A (H5Nx) using plasma samples from the CRCHUM Health Care Workers cohort in Montreal, Canada, during the 2024 influenza seasonal vaccination. The capacity of their plasma to recognize hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) antigens from ten influenza strains was measured. Their neutralizing activity, as well as their capacity to mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) against cells stably expressing HA and NA, was measured. Overall, seasonal vaccination against H1N1/H3N2 elicited antibodies able to recognize several HA and NA, and in some individuals, this translated to increased neutralization and ADCC activity, including against H5Nx. This study provides insightful information on how vaccination shapes cross-reactive antibody responses against avian H5Nx. IMPORTANCE: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are endemic in the human population and responsible for hundreds of thousands of deaths every year, occasionally leading to influenza pandemics. Since 2023, there has been a rise in avian IAV infections in humans, with some deaths reported, mostly related to the H5N1 subtype clade 2.3.4.4b. Seasonal vaccines against IAVs are effective, but their efficacy against avian IAVs is not well known. Here, following influenza seasonal vaccination in a cohort of adults, we report highly heterogeneous serological responses, possibly due to pre-existing immunity and HA sequence similarity. These findings provide insight into the breadth of pre-existing and vaccine-induced immunity against H5 influenza viruses and may inform the development of vaccination strategies aimed at providing broader protection against emerging influenza viruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate whether seasonal influenza vaccination could elicit cross-reactive antibodies against avian influenza A (H5Nx) subtypes, given the uncertainty surrounding its capacity to do so. The background highlights the importance of understanding cross-subtype immunity as avian influenza infections in humans have increased since 2023.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using plasma samples from the CRCHUM Health Care Workers cohort in Montreal, Canada, following the 2024 influenza seasonal vaccination. The design involved measuring serological responses against seasonal (H1N1/H3N2) and avian subtypes A (H5Nx) in a cohort of adults.
analysis.methods: Antibody responses were measured against hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) antigens from ten influenza strains. Neutralizing activity and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) against cells expressing HA and NA were also assessed.
analysis.main_results: Seasonal vaccination against H1N1/H3N2 elicited antibodies that recognized several HA and NA antigens, and in some individuals, this translated to increased neutralization and ADCC activity, including against H5Nx.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that seasonal vaccination can induce cross-reactive immunity against avian H5Nx, which may have implications for broader protection against emerging influenza viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of vaccination strategies that enhance cross-protection against avian influenza viruses, particularly in light of the recent rise in human infections with H5N1.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single cohort and does not account for long-term immunity or broader population data. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on serological responses measured in a specific group of health care workers.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether seasonal influenza vaccination against H1N1/H3N2 could elicit cross-reactive antibodies against avian influenza A (H5Nx) subtypes. Using plasma samples from health care workers in Montreal, Canada, following the 2024 vaccination campaign, the researchers measured antibody responses against HA and NA antigens from ten influenza strains. They found that seasonal vaccination induced antibodies capable of recognizing several HA and NA antigens, with some individuals showing increased neutralization and ADCC activity against H5Nx. These results suggest that seasonal vaccines may offer some cross-protection against avian influenza viruses, which is relevant given the recent rise in human infections with H5N1. However, the study is limited to a specific cohort and does not provide long-term or population-level data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查 季节性流感 疫苗接种 是否可以引发针对甲型禽流感 (H5Nx) 亚型的交叉反应抗体,因为其能力存在不确定性。这一背景凸显了了解跨亚型免疫的重要性,因为自 2023 年以来人类禽流感感染有所增加。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在 2024 年季节性流感 疫苗接种 之后使用来自加拿大蒙特利尔 CRCHUM 卫生保健工作者 队列研究 的血浆样本进行的。该设计涉及测量 队列研究 成人针对季节性 (H1N1/H3N2) 和禽类 A 亚型 (H5Nx) 的血清学反应。
elements_zh.methods: 测量了针对十种流感病毒株的血凝素 (HA) 和神经氨酸酶 (NA) 抗原的抗体反应。还评估了针对表达 HA 和 NA 的细胞的中和活性和抗体依赖性细胞毒性 (ADCC)。
elements_zh.main_results: 针对 H1N1/H3N2 的季节性 疫苗接种 引发了识别多种 HA 和 NA 抗原的抗体,在某些个体中,这转化为中和和 ADCC 活性的增加,包括针对 H5Nx 的抗体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,季节性 疫苗接种 可以诱导针对禽类 H5Nx 的交叉反应免疫,这可能对更广泛地预防新出现的流感病毒产生影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能为 疫苗接种 策略的制定提供信息,以增强针对禽流感病毒的交叉保护,特别是考虑到最近人类 H5N1 感染的增加。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单个 队列研究,并未考虑长期免疫或更广泛的人群数据。证据是温和的,因为它是基于在特定的医护人员群体中测量的血清学反应。

papers.title: Matrix Metalloproteinase-8 Deficiency Alters the Balance Between Viral Clearance and Immunopathology in H1N1 Infection.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Matrix metalloproteinase‐8 (MMP‐8) regulates inflammatory responses, but its contributions to the pathogenesis of influenza A viral (IAV) disease are not known. Plasma MMP‐8 levels were increased 30‐fold in subjects infected with H1N1 or seasonal IAV and were inversely associated with the PaO 2 /FiO 2 ratio, suggesting potential value as a candidate marker of lung injury severity that requires validation in larger cohorts. MMP‐8 levels were elevated in the lungs of H1N1‐infected wild‐type (WT) mice and localized to airway epithelial cells, macrophages, and polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs). H1N1‐infected Mmp‐8 −/− mice exhibited lower mortality and reduced lung viral burdens, but developed more severe lung injury than WT mice. Gene expression profiling revealed enhanced necroptosis and an exaggerated immune response in the lungs of infected Mmp‐8 −/− mice. Infected Mmp‐8 −/− mice had increased airway epithelial necroptosis with higher pulmonary levels of Type I interferons (IFNs), and increased frequencies of Class II MHC molecule‐expressing macrophages and CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, and higher levels of some Th1 cytokines. In vitro, MMP‐8 cleaved IL‐1β and IL‐6, but not Type I IFNs. These findings suggest that Mmp‐8 deficiency is associated with restricted influenza virus spread and increased lung injury, accompanied by enhanced Type I IFN‐associated necroptotic signaling and augmented antiviral immune responses. The latter may partly involve loss of MMP‐8‐mediated processing of pro‐inflammatory mediators. MMP‐8 may represent a host‐response target in severe influenza infection, although therapeutic strategies targeting MMP‐8 will need to balance enhanced viral clearance against the risk of increased lung immunopathology.

analysis.methods: MMP-8 levels were measured in the lungs and plasma of infected mice, and gene expression profiling was used to analyze immune responses. In vitro experiments were conducted to assess MMP-8's ability to cleave specific cytokines.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of targeted therapies that modulate host responses to balance viral clearance and immunopathology in severe influenza cases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of Matrix Metalloproteinase-8 (MMP-8) in influenza A viral (IAV) disease, focusing on its impact on viral clearance and immunopathology. Using H1N1-infected wild-type (WT) and Mmp-8 −/− mice, the research found that MMP-8 deficiency reduced mortality and viral burden but increased lung injury. Plasma MMP-8 levels were elevated in IAV-infected subjects and inversely correlated with lung injury severity. In vitro experiments showed MMP-8 cleaves IL-1β and IL-6 but not Type I interferons. The study suggests MMP-8 could be a host-response target for therapies in severe influenza, though further human studies are needed. The evidence is moderate due to reliance on animal models and limited direct human data.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨基质金属蛋白酶-8(MMP-8)在流感病毒A(IAV)疾病发病机制中的作用,因为其在炎症反应和病毒感染结果中的贡献此前尚不清楚。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及H1N1感染的野生型(WT)小鼠和Mmp-8 −/−小鼠,比较它们在死亡率、病毒载量和肺损伤方面的结果。同时,还评估了感染H1N1或季节性IAV的受试者血浆中MMP-8的水平。
analysis_zh.methods: 测量了感染小鼠肺部和血浆中的MMP-8水平,并利用基因表达分析来研究免疫应答。进行了体外实验以评估MMP-8对特定细胞因子的切割能力。
analysis_zh.main_results: H1N1感染的Mmp-8 −/−小鼠表现出较低的死亡率和较低的肺病毒载量,但与WT小鼠相比,肺损伤更为严重。感染H1N1或季节性IAV的受试者血浆中MMP-8水平升高了30倍,并且与PaO2/FiO2比值呈反向关联。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,MMP-8缺乏可能导致病毒传播受限但肺部免疫病理增加,突显了其作为宿主反应靶点的潜力,为严重流感感染的治疗策略提供了新的思路。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能有助于开发针对宿主反应的靶向疗法,以在严重流感病例中平衡病毒清除与免疫病理。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于动物模型和体外实验,可能无法完全反映人类结果。证据强度中等,因为它基于单一研究,没有直接的人类临床数据。

papers.title: Influenza vaccine effectiveness against hospitalization in children aged 6–72 months: a test-negative study in the Southern Italy, 2022–2026
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza is an important cause of hospitalization in young children, yet real-world evidence on vaccine effectiveness (VE) against severe outcomes remains limited in Italy. We estimated influenza VE against influenza-associated hospitalization among children aged 6-72 months in the district of Foggia, Southern Italy. METHODS: We conducted a test-negative case-control study among children hospitalized for acute respiratory infection and tested for influenza during the 2022-2023 to 2025-2026 influenza seasons. Cases were influenza-positive children and controls were influenza-negative children. VE was estimated as (1 - odds ratio) x 100; adjusted VE was derived from multivariable logistic regression models. RESULTS: The study included 935 children, of whom 207 were influenza-positive cases and 728 were influenza-negative controls. Adjusted VE was 62.5% (95% CI: 34.4%-78.5%) for receipt of at least one influenza vaccine dose and 61.9% (95% CI: 29.3%-79.4%) for full vaccination. By vaccine type, adjusted VE was 80.3% (95% CI: 43.8%-93.1%) for at least one dose of LAIV and 50.9% (95% CI: 6.9%-74.2%) for at least one dose of IIV. Season-specific adjusted VE was highest in 2024-2025, reaching 92.2% (95% CI: 65.6%-98.2%) for at least one dose and 90.7% (95% CI: 58.5%-97.9%) for full vaccination. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza vaccination was associated with a reduced risk of influenza-associated hospitalization among children aged 6-72 months, with the strongest protection observed during the 2024-2025 season. These findings support continued efforts to improve pediatric influenza vaccination uptake.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of influenza vaccines against hospitalization due to influenza in children aged 6–72 months in Southern Italy. A test-negative case-control study was conducted during the 2022–2023 to 2025–2026 influenza seasons, comparing influenza-positive and -negative children. The results showed that adjusted vaccine effectiveness (VE) was 62.5% for at least one dose and 61.9% for full vaccination. By vaccine type, VE was 80.3% for live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) and 50.9% for inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV). Season-specific VE was highest in 2024–2025, reaching 92.2% for at least one dose and 90.7% for full vaccination. The findings suggest that influenza vaccination reduces the risk of hospitalization in children, with stronger protection observed during certain seasons. These results support efforts to increase vaccination rates in this population. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the study design and the absence of reported limitations.

analysis_zh.main_results: 研究共纳入935名儿童,其中207名是流感阳性病例,728名是流感阴性对照。按疫苗类型分析,至少接种一剂LAIV的调整后VE为80.3%(95% CI:43.8%-93.1%),至少接种一剂IIV的调整后VE为50.9%(95% CI:6.9%-74.2%)。按季节分析,2024-2025年的调整后VE最高,至少接种一剂的VE达到92.2%(95% CI:65.6%-98.2%),完成疫苗接种接种的VE达到90.7%(95% CI:58.5%-97.9%)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 疫苗接种疫苗与6-72个月儿童流感相关住院风险降低相关,其中2024-2025年流感季节的保护效果最强。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持继续努力提高儿童流感疫苗接种率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告该研究的具体局限性。

papers.title: Economic analysis of adjuvanted trivalent influenza vaccine for older adults in the Korean National Immunization Program
papers.abstract: Background Seasonal influenza causes substantial morbidity and mortality among older adults in South Korea despite high vaccination coverage. The MF59-adjuvanted trivalent influenza vaccine (aTIV) has shown superior immunogenicity in older populations, but its economic value within the Korean National Immunization Program (NIP) has not been evaluated using a dynamic transmission model that captures indirect protection. This study evaluated the budget impact of introducing aTIV into the Korean NIP for adults aged ≥65 years. Methods We developed an age-structured dynamic compartmental model to simulate seasonal influenza transmission in South Korea, allowing estimation of both direct and indirect protection effects. From the healthcare payer perspective and over a single influenza season, we performed a budget impact analysis complemented by a cost–benefit comparison of avoided medical costs against incremental vaccination expenditures. Two aTIV strategies were compared against standard quadrivalent influenza vaccine (QIV) within the NIP framework: Strategy I (aTIV for adults aged ≥75 years) and Strategy II (aTIV for all adults aged ≥65 years). Deterministic one-way sensitivity analyses examined relative vaccine effectiveness (rVE) of aTIV versus QIV across 5–30% and seasonal attack rate across ±20% of the 8.0% baseline, and a break-even analysis identified the rVE threshold at which incremental costs equal avoided treatment costs. A probabilistic sensitivity analysis was also conducted to quantify joint parameter uncertainty. Results At baseline (rVE 25%, attack rate 8.0%), Strategy I required $24.6 million in additional vaccine investment, with 52% offset by treatment savings, yielding a net budget impact of $11.7 million (+0.9% of total influenza-related healthcare expenditure). Strategy II required $54.4 million in additional costs with 57% offset ($31.2 million in savings), resulting in a net impact of $23.2 million (+1.8%). Strategy II prevented 535 deaths and over 15,000 hospitalizations—2.2-fold greater than Strategy I. The incremental cost of aTIV decreased with increasing transmission intensity, approaching cost neutrality during severe epidemic seasons. The break-even rVE at which aTIV becomes cost-saving was 44%, above central meta-analytic estimates (10–25%) but potentially attainable in severe seasons or specific subpopulations. Conclusion Introduction of aTIV into the Korean NIP is budget-feasible with substantial health benefits, requiring only a 0.9–1.8% increase in total influenza-related healthcare expenditure. At current rVE estimates (≤30%), aTIV does not achieve cost savings, but the additional fiscal burden remains modest. Strategy II offers superior health outcome value and is preferred when budget permits, while Strategy I provides a fiscally conservative entry point. The value proposition of aTIV is most favorable during severe influenza seasons.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管韩国老年人流感疫苗接种覆盖率较高,但季节性流感仍导致显著的发病率和死亡率。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了在韩国国家免疫接种计划中引入aTIV对≥65岁成年人的预算影响。
elements_zh.methods: 我们开发了一个年龄结构化的动态分室模型,用于模拟韩国的季节性流感 传播,从而能够估算直接和间接保护效应。从卫生保健支付者的视角出发,针对一个流感季节,我们进行了预算影响分析,并结合避免医疗费用与增量疫苗接种支出的成本-效益比较。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在韩国国家免疫接种计划中引入aTIV是预算可行的,具有显著的健康效益,仅需将总流感相关卫生支出增加0.9-1.8%。

papers.title: Molecular evolution and epitope landscape of influenza A(H1N1) viruses in Iran: insights from whole-genome sequencing (2023–2025)
papers.abstract: Influenza viruses continuously evolve, resulting in genetic diversity that contributes to influenza epidemics and pandemics. This high mutation rate increases the probability of immune evasion, thereby reducing vaccine effectiveness. This study aimed to investigate the genomic and molecular changes in influenza A/H1N1 viruses during 2023–2025. In this study, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of 30 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 strains circulating in Iran during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons was performed using Oxford Nanopore Technology. Subsequently, genomic, molecular, and phylogenetic analyses were performed, and vaccine efficacy was estimated using the epitope method. Whole-genome sequencing of influenza A/H1N1 viruses revealed that the strains circulating during the 2024–2025 season had a slightly lower similarity to the vaccine strain (98.78%) than those circulating during the 2023–2024 season (99.13%). Epitope A was the most diverse region during both seasons, with estimated vaccine efficacy against the dominant epitope ranging from 38.1% to 50.5% during 2023–2025. Several substitutions were identified in the internal proteins, of which the virulence-associated I123V substitution in NS1 was detected in both the vaccine and analyzed strains. Moreover, the studied strains remained largely susceptible to neuraminidase inhibitors, although one strain carried the S247N substitution. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that 90% of Iranian strains clustered within the 6B.1 A.5a.2a clade, which included globally circulating viruses from the same seasons. Despite topological differences among the phylogenetic trees, no reassortment was detected. The epitope landscape of Iranian A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses circulating during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 influenza seasons showed that their genetic makeup underwent seasonal changes due to antigenic drift in HA and NA. Despite these changes, the circulating strains remained closely related to the corresponding vaccine strain, and the estimated vaccine efficacy against the epitopes with the highest number of substitutions was acceptable, consistent with the WHO recommendation to retain A/Wisconsin/67/2022 for the 2025–2026 seasonal vaccine. This study emphasizes the importance of national influenza surveillance within global frameworks to monitor antigenic changes, assess pandemic risks, guide vaccine strain selection, and evaluate antiviral resistance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the genomic and molecular changes in influenza A/H1N1 viruses during 2023–2025. Influenza viruses continuously evolve, resulting in genetic diversity that contributes to influenza epidemics and pandemics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of 30 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 strains circulating in Iran during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons was performed. The study focused on seasonal influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses and their molecular evolution.
analysis.methods: Whole-genome sequencing of influenza A/H1N1 viruses revealed that the strains circulating during the 2024–2025 season had a slightly lower similarity to the vaccine strain (98.78%) than those circulating during the 2023–2024 season (99.13%). Genomic, molecular, and phylogenetic analyses were performed, and vaccine efficacy was estimated using the epitope method.
analysis.main_results: Several substitutions were identified in the internal proteins, of which the virulence-associated I123V substitution in NS1 was detected in both the vaccine and analyzed strains. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that 90% of Iranian strains clustered within the 6B.1 A.5a.2a clade, which included globally circulating viruses from the same seasons. The epitope landscape of Iranian A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses showed that their genetic makeup underwent seasonal changes due to antigenic drift in HA and NA.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the seasonal genetic changes in influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses and their implications for vaccine efficacy. Despite these changes, the circulating strains remained closely related to the corresponding vaccine strain, and the estimated vaccine efficacy against the epitopes with the highest number of substitutions was acceptable.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study emphasizes the importance of national influenza surveillance within global frameworks to monitor antigenic changes, assess pandemic risks, guide vaccine strain selection, and evaluate antiviral resistance. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on whole-genome sequencing of a limited number of strains, which may not fully represent the genetic diversity of the entire population. The study underscores the importance of national surveillance to monitor antigenic changes and guide vaccine strain selection. However, the findings are based on a limited sample and abstract-only data, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

papers.title_zh: 伊朗甲型H1N1流感病毒的分子进化和表位景观:基于全基因组基因组测序(2023–2025)的见解
papers.source_body_en: Influenza viruses continuously evolve, resulting in genetic diversity that contributes to influenza epidemics and pandemics. This high mutation rate increases the probability of immune evasion, thereby reducing vaccine effectiveness. This study aimed to investigate the genomic and molecular changes in influenza A/H1N1 viruses during 2023–2025. In this study, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of 30 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 strains circulating in Iran during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons was performed using Oxford Nanopore Technology. Subsequently, genomic, molecular, and phylogenetic analyses were performed, and vaccine efficacy was estimated using the epitope method. Whole-genome sequencing of influenza A/H1N1 viruses revealed that the strains circulating during the 2024–2025 season had a slightly lower similarity to the vaccine strain (98.78%) than those circulating during the 2023–2024 season (99.13%). Epitope A was the most diverse region during both seasons, with estimated vaccine efficacy against the dominant epitope ranging from 38.1% to 50.5% during 2023–2025. Several substitutions were identified in the internal proteins, of which the virulence-associated I123V substitution in NS1 was detected in both the vaccine and analyzed strains. Moreover, the studied strains remained largely susceptible to neuraminidase inhibitors, although one strain carried the S247N substitution. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that 90% of Iranian strains clustered within the 6B.1 A.5a.2a clade, which included globally circulating viruses from the same seasons. Despite topological differences among the phylogenetic trees, no reassortment was detected. The epitope landscape of Iranian A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses circulating during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 influenza seasons showed that their genetic makeup underwent seasonal changes due to antigenic drift in HA and NA. Despite these changes, the circulating strains remained closely related to the corresponding vaccine strain, and the estimated vaccine efficacy against the epitopes with the highest number of substitutions was acceptable, consistent with the WHO recommendation to retain A/Wisconsin/67/2022 for the 2025–2026 seasonal vaccine. This study emphasizes the importance of national influenza surveillance within global frameworks to monitor antigenic changes, assess pandemic risks, guide vaccine strain selection, and evaluate antiviral resistance.
papers.abstract_zh: 流感病毒持续进化,导致遗传多样性,这有助于流感的流行和大流行。这种高进化速率增加了免疫逃逸的可能性,从而降低了疫苗有效性。本研究旨在调查2023–2025年间流感A/H1N1病毒的基因组和分子变化。本研究使用牛津纳米孔技术对伊朗2023–2024和2024–2025流感季节中流行的30株流感病毒进行了全基因组测序(WGS)。随后进行了基因组、分子和系统发育分析,并利用表位方法估计了疫苗有效性。流感A/H1N1病毒的全基因组测序显示,2024–2025流感季节流行的病毒株与疫苗株的相似性略低于2023–2024流感季节流行的病毒株(98.78% vs. 99.13%)。在两个流感季节中,表位A是最具多样性的区域,2023–2025年间针对主要表位的疫苗有效性估计为38.1%至50.5%。在内部蛋白中发现了几种取代,其中NS1蛋白与致病性相关的I123V取代在疫苗株和分析株中均被检测到。此外,所研究的病毒株总体上仍对神经氨酸酶抑制剂敏感,尽管有一株携带S247N取代。系统发育分析显示,90%的伊朗病毒株聚类在6B.1 A.5a.2a谱系中,该谱系包括了同一季节全球流行的病毒株。尽管系统发育树之间存在拓扑差异,但未检测到基因重配。伊朗2023–2024和2024–2025流感季节流行的甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09病毒的表位景观显示,其遗传组成因HA和NA中的突变而发生了季节性变化。尽管有这些变化,流行的病毒株仍与相应的疫苗株密切相关,针对突变最多的表位的疫苗有效性估计是可接受的,符合世界卫生组织保留A/Wisconsin/67/2022作为2025–2026季节性疫苗的建议。本研究强调了在国际框架下进行国家流感监测的重要性,以监测抗原变化、评估大流行风险、指导疫苗株选择以及评估抗病毒药物耐药性。

papers.title: Influenza vaccine protection and contact patterns among outpatients with influenza-like illness during the 2024-2025 season in China: a test-negative case-control study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Continuous monitoring of both influenza vaccine protection and behavioural determinants of infection is important for understanding related risks. Evidence on influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in China during the 2024-2025 season, however, remains limited. We aimed to assess influenza VE among healthcare-seeking outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) and to examine the contact patterns associated with infection risk. METHODS: We enrolled 928 outpatients with ILI from three sentinel hospitals in Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture, China, between December 2024 and March 2025 in a test-negative case-control study. We confirmed influenza infection using reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction and collected vaccination history and social contact frequency and duration through questionnaires. We estimated VE using logistic regression with covariate adjustment, and otherwise analysed social contact patterns and performed exploratory sequencing of six randomly selected influenza-positive samples. RESULTS: Our full sample comprised 928 participants. We excluded 21 infants younger than 6 months from the VE analysis and included 907 participants, of whom 121 tested positive and 786 tested negative. The overall adjusted VE against medically attended influenza was 42.3% (95% credible interval = 11.1-62.5). In the analysis of social contacts for all 928 participants, test-positive children aged 0-10 years and adults aged 65 years or older reported more frequent and longer social contact than their test-negative counterparts. Exploratory sequencing of six samples suggested no major antigenic mismatch with the vaccine strains, but the very small number of sequenced samples limits the generalisability of this finding. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza vaccination provided moderate protection against medically attended influenza, while contact patterns were associated with infection risk among children and older adults. Combined vaccination and behavioural interventions warrant further evaluation, as the observational design of this study and its use of self-reporting data limit causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) among healthcare-seeking outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) and examine contact patterns associated with infection risk during the 2024-2025 season in China. A test-negative case-control study was conducted at three sentinel hospitals in Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture, enrolling 928 participants. Influenza infection was confirmed using reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, and vaccination history and social contact data were collected via questionnaires. The overall adjusted VE against medically attended influenza was 42.3% (95% credible interval = 11.1-62.5). These results suggest the need for combined vaccination and behavioural interventions to reduce influenza transmission.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 持续监测流感疫苗保护效果和感染行为决定因素对于理解相关风险至关重要。然而,目前关于2024-2025流感季中国流感疫苗有效性(VE)的证据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们在2024年12月至2025年3月期间,从中国伊犁哈萨克自治州的三家哨点医院招募了928名流感样病例(ILI)门诊患者,进行一项测试阴性病例对照研究。我们排除了21名小于6个月的婴儿进行VE分析,并纳入了907名参与者,其中121人检测为阳性,786人检测为阴性。
elements_zh.methods: 我们通过逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)确认流感感染,并通过问卷收集疫苗接种接种史、社会接触频率和持续时间。我们使用带有协变量调整的逻辑回归模型来估计VE,并对社会接触模式进行分析,同时对六份随机选取的流感阳性样本进行探索性测序。
elements_zh.main_results: 我们的完整样本包括928名参与者。针对医疗就诊流感的调整后总体VE为42.3%(95%可信区间=11.1-62.5)。在对所有928名参与者的社会接触分析中,检测为阳性的0-10岁儿童和65岁及以上成年人报告的社会接触频率和持续时间均高于检测为阴性的对应人群。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 流感疫苗接种对医疗就诊流感提供了中等程度的保护,而接触模式与儿童和老年人的感染风险相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结合疫苗接种和行为干预措施需要进一步评估,因为本研究的观察性设计及其使用自我报告数据限制了因果推论的得出。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 六份样本的探索性测序表明,与疫苗毒株之间没有显著的抗原差异,但测序样本数量非常有限,限制了这一发现的普遍适用性。研究的观察性设计及其使用自我报告数据限制了因果推论的得出。

We estimated VE using logistic regression with covariate adjustment, and otherwise analysed social contact patterns and performed exploratory sequencing of six randomly selected influenza-positive samples. RESULTS: Our full sample comprised 928 participants. We excluded 21 infants younger than 6 months from the VE analysis and included 907 participants, of whom 121 tested positive and 786 tested negative. The overall adjusted VE against medically attended influenza was 42.3% (95% credible interval = 11.1-62.5). In the analysis of social contacts for all 928 participants, test-positive children aged 0-10 years and adults aged 65 years or older reported more frequent and longer social contact than their test-negative counterparts. Exploratory sequencing of six samples suggested no major antigenic mismatch with the vaccine strains, but the very small number of sequenced samples limits the generalisability of this finding. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza vaccination provided moderate protection against medically attended influenza, while contact patterns were associated with infection risk among children and older adults. Combined vaccination and behavioural interventions warrant further evaluation, as the observational design of this study and its use of self-reporting data limit causal inference.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:持续监测流感疫苗保护效果和感染行为决定因素对于理解相关风险至关重要。然而,目前关于2024-2025流感季中国流感疫苗有效性(VE)的证据仍然有限。我们旨在评估流感疫苗在寻求医疗帮助的流感样病例(ILI)门诊患者中的有效性,并探讨与感染风险相关的接触模式。方法:我们在2024年12月至2025年3月期间,从中国伊犁哈萨克自治州的三家哨点医院招募了928名流感样病例门诊患者,进行一项测试阴性病例对照研究。我们通过逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)确认流感感染,并通过问卷收集疫苗接种接种史、社会接触频率和持续时间。我们使用带有协变量调整的逻辑回归模型来估计VE,并对社会接触模式进行分析,同时对六份随机选取的流感阳性样本进行探索性测序。结果:我们的完整样本包括928名参与者。在VE分析中,我们排除了21名小于6个月的婴儿,最终纳入907名参与者,其中121人检测为阳性,786人检测为阴性。针对医疗就诊流感的调整后总体VE为42.3%(95%可信区间=11.1-62.5)。在对所有928名参与者的社会接触分析中,检测为阳性的0-10岁儿童和65岁及以上成年人报告的社会接触频率和持续时间均高于检测为阴性的对应人群。六份样本的探索性测序表明,与疫苗毒株之间没有显著的抗原差异,但测序样本数量非常有限,限制了这一发现的普遍适用性。结论:流感疫苗接种对医疗就诊流感提供了中等程度的保护,而接触模式与儿童和老年人的感染风险相关。结合疫苗接种和行为干预措施需要进一步评估,因为本研究的观察性设计及其使用自我报告数据限制了因果推论的得出。科学与公共卫生意义:结合疫苗接种和行为干预措施需要进一步评估,因为本研究的观察性设计及其使用自我报告数据限制了因果推论的得出。局限性与证据强度:六份样本的探索性测序表明,与疫苗毒株之间没有显著的抗原差异,但测序样本数量非常有限,限制了这一发现的普遍适用性。研究的观察性设计及其使用自我报告数据限制了因果推论的得出。

papers.title: Trends in long COVID and post-viral fatigue in children in primary care in England
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-viral sequelae following the COVID-19 pandemic attention to post-viral fatigue and long COVID, but the impact on children and young people's (CYP) primary care use is unknown. AIM: To examine temporal, seasonal, and sociodemographic patterns in primary care consultations for long COVID and PVFS in CYP DESIGN AND SETTINGS: We conducted a retrospective, population-based dynamic cohort study using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum data for CYP aged <18 years in England, between 1st January 2006 and 31st December 2022 (from 1st March 2020 for long COVID); a period covering the influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and COVID-19 pandemics. METHOD: Consultation rates per 100 000 child-years were calculated for long COVID and post-viral fatigue syndrome (PVFS) by calendar year, month, and sociodemographic characteristics. Trends, seasonal patterns, and differences between pandemic and non-pandemic periods (for PVFS) were described. Negative binomial regression was used to estimate associations with sociodemographic characteristics. RESULTS: The cohort included 7,442,572 CYP (3 624 692 registered in primary care during the COVID-19 pandemic). There were 6700 long COVID and 20,440 PVFS consultations. Long COVID consultation rates were highest in 2022 (140.3 per 100,00 child-years). PVFS consultation rates peaked in 2009 and 2022 (during H1N1 and COVID pandemics) with rates of 57.1 and 56.9 per 100 000 child-years, respectively. Consultation rates were highest among older CYP, girls, and those from least deprived areas. CONCLUSION: Long COVID consultations were highest in 2022, and PVFS consultation rates peaked during 2009 and 2022. Our findings that rates were highest in less deprived areas and girls need further investigation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of understanding about the impact of post-viral sequelae, specifically long COVID and post-viral fatigue syndrome (PVFS), on children and young people's (CYP) primary care use.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, population-based dynamic cohort study was conducted using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum data for CYP aged <18 years in England, between 1st January 2006 and 31st December 2022, with a focus on the period from 1st March 2020 onwards for long COVID.
analysis.methods: Negative binomial regression was used to estimate associations between sociodemographic characteristics and consultation rates for long COVID and PVFS.
analysis.main_results: The study found 6700 long COVID and 20,440 PVFS consultations. Long COVID consultation rates were highest in 2022 at 140.3 per 100,000 child-years, while PVFS consultation rates peaked in 2009 and 2022 at 57.1 and 56.9 per 100,000 child-years, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the highest consultation rates for long COVID and PVFS were observed during the pandemic and the H1N1 outbreak, and noted that the findings regarding higher rates in less deprived areas and among girls require further investigation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and resource allocation in primary care for post-viral conditions, particularly during influenza pandemics, highlighting the need for targeted support in specific sociodemographic groups.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on existing data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations and the focus on observed consultation rates without causal analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines trends in long COVID and post-viral fatigue syndrome (PVFS) consultations in children and young people (CYP) in England between 2006 and 2022. It highlights that long COVID consultation rates were highest in 2022, while PVFS rates peaked during the 2009 H1N1 pandemic and the 2022 COVID-19 pandemic. The research identifies higher consultation rates among older CYP, girls, and those from less deprived areas, suggesting potential sociodemographic patterns. The study's findings are relevant for understanding the impact of post-viral conditions on primary care use and may guide future surveillance and resource allocation. However, the retrospective design and reliance on existing data limit the confidence in the results, leading to a moderate evidence assessment.
