full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractBackgroundContinuous monitoring of both influenza vaccine protection and behavioural determinants of infection is important for understanding related risks. Evidence on influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in China during the 2024–2025 season, however, remains limited. We aimed to assess influenza VE among healthcare-seeking outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) and to examine the contact patterns associated with infection risk.MethodsWe enrolled 928 outpatients with ILI from three sentinel hospitals in Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture, China, between December 2024 and March 2025 in a test-negative case-control study. We confirmed influenza infection using reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction and collected vaccination history and social contact frequency and duration through questionnaires. We estimated VE using logistic regression with covariate adjustment, and otherwise analysed social contact patterns and performed exploratory sequencing of six randomly selected influenza-positive samples.ResultsOur full sample comprised 928 participants. We excluded 21 infants younger than 6 months from the VE analysis and included 907 participants, of whom 121 tested positive and 786 tested negative. The overall adjusted VE against medically attended influenza was 42.3% (95% credible interval = 11.1–62.5). In the analysis of social contacts for all 928 participants, test-positive children aged 0–10 years and adults aged 65 years or older reported more frequent and longer social contact than their test-negative counterparts. Exploratory sequencing of six samples suggested no major antigenic mismatch with the vaccine strains, but the very small number of sequenced samples limits the generalisability of this finding.ConclusionsInfluenza vaccination provided moderate protection against medically attended influenza, while contact patterns were associated with infection risk among children and older adults. Combined vaccination and behavioural interventions warrant further evaluation, as the observational design of this study and its use of self-reporting data limit causal inference.Keywords : influenza, influenza vaccination, vaccine effectiveness, test-negative design, contact patterns, China
full_text_sections.methods: METHODSSetting and study designWe conducted a multicentre test-negative case-control study from 8 December 2024 (epidemiological week 50) to 30 March 2025 (epidemiological week 13) among outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) from three sentinel hospitals in Yining and Horgos, Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture, China. These sentinel outpatient clinics serve as the core data source for the national influenza surveillance network and support the systematic collection of epidemiological and virological data.In accordance with the Chinese National Influenza Surveillance Protocol, we defined ILI as the presence of fever (body temperature ≥38°C) accompanied by a cough or sore throat [33]. We randomly selected 10–40 patients (typically 20) with ILI each week from whom we collected nasal or nasopharyngeal specimens for influenza testing using real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), and administered a structured questionnaire to collect demographic information, influenza vaccination history, and social contact patterns. Trained hospital staff administered structured questionnaires and recorded the responses in an electronic database. We linked the questionnaire records to the corresponding laboratory results using unique study identifiers.We included outpatients who presented with ILI at a sentinel hospital, understood the questionnaire, and provided verbal informed consent, either personally or through a guardian. We excluded participants younger than six months of age from the VE analysis because maternal antibodies could provide protection. We truncated the number of reported daily contact counts above 30 at 30 in the contact analysis to reduce the influence of outliers.Outcome variableWe defined the influenza test result as a dichotomous variable, categorised as positive or negative based on RT-PCR analysis of nasopharyngeal swab specimens. We performed testing using the Zhuocheng Huisheng Influenza A/B Duplex real-time PCR detection kit (Beijing Zhuocheng Huisheng Bioscience Co., Ltd., Beijing, China). This kit used specific primers and fluorescent probes targeting influenza A and B viruses and included an internal control that monitors the entire process from nucleic acid extraction to amplification, thereby reducing the risk of false-negative results.Exposure variablesWe defined influenza vaccination status as the primary exposure variable based on data reported by the participants or their guardians. We classified participants as vaccinated if they had received at least one dose of a seasonal influenza vaccine, including egg-based, cell-based, trivalent, and quadrivalent vaccines, within the past 24 months, with the most recent dose being administered at least 14 days before symptom onset. We classified participants who did not meet these criteria as unvaccinated.We defined social contact pattern as the secondary exposure variable and characterised it by contact frequency and duration according to the POLYMOD study criteria [22]. We defined conversational contact as a face-to-face conversation with an exchange of at least three words, and physical contact as any skin-to-skin interaction, such as handshaking, hugging, or kissing.CovariatesWe collected potential confounders using structured questionnaires (Text S1 in the Online Supplementary Document), including demographic characteristics such as age, sex, and ethnicity; clinical and behavioural characteristics, such as baseline health conditions, health-related behaviours, and daily habits; and temporal variables, such as the dates of symptom onset and visit dates. We grouped age for further analysis and used symptom onset and visit dates to derive the epidemiological week for adjustment for long-term and seasonal trends.Viral sequencing sample selection and reference sequencesThe national Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) influenza surveillance protocol requires sentinel hospitals to perform viral genetic sequencing on a subset of influenza-positive samples during routine surveillance to monitor genetic variation among circulating strains, rather than sequencing all positive samples [33]. We selected 6 out of 121 influenza-positive samples for exploratory sequencing in accordance with this protocol.We retrieved global influenza A(H1N1) reference sequences from the Global Initiative on Sharing All Influenza Data (GISAID) database [34]. We selected 170 sequences containing both haemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) gene segments and combined them with six viral isolates obtained in this study.Statistical analysisWe used a Bayesian logistic regression model adjusted for covariates to estimate VE. We specified an informative prior for the vaccination coefficient, centred on a VE of 40% based on historical CDC estimates [35]. We calculated VE for laboratory-confirmed influenza as (1 − odds ratio) × 100% and expressed uncertainty in the model coefficients using 95% credible intervals (CrIs) derived from the posterior distribution.We performed targeted sequencing of 6 virus isolates from influenza-positive participants and conducted phylogenetic analysis together with 170 reference sequences retrieved from GISAID. We aligned the sequences using ClustalW in Molecular Evolutionary Genetics Analysis, version 12 [36] and assessed alignment quality using ESPript [37]. We constructed a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree using IQ-TREE [38]. We then compared sequences within a specific monophyletic clade to identify variable sites and non-synonymous mutations (Text S3 in the Online Supplementary Document).We performed age standardisation according to the 2020 China Population Census. We used linear regression to quantify age-specific differences in contact frequency and duration (β) between influenza test-positive and test-negative participants. We smoothed the contact matrices using Gaussian kernel density estimation. We used stratified χ2 tests to compare the distributions of contact setting, frequency, and duration between the groups. We used a Bayesian negative binomial regression model to assess the effects of demographic characteristics and contact setting and evaluated model robustness against a gamma model (Text S4 in the Online Supplementary Document).We conducted subgroup analyses for VE by age group (6 months to 6 years, 7–17 years, 18–59 years, and ≥60 years) and influenza subtype (A(H1), A(H3), and B/Victoria). We performed similar analyses for social contacts by age groups (0–5 years, 6–15 years, 16–65 years, and >65 years) based on immune status, social behaviours, and health risks, with further stratification by sex (male and female), household size (small, ≤3 persons; medium, 4 persons; large, ≥5 persons), and contact setting (home, school, workplace, leisure, and other) (Text S4 in the Online Supplementary Document).We also conducted sensitivity analyses to evaluate the robustness of the VE estimates and social contact analyses (Text S5 in the Online Supplementary Document). For the VE analysis, we assessed the effects of including infants younger than six months, treating age and body mass index as continuous variables, and adjusting for the symptom onset date. For the social contact analysis, we restricted the sample to unvaccinated participants to reduce potential confounding by vaccination status.We performed all statistical analyses and phylogenetic tree visualisations using R, version 4.3.2 (R Core Team, Vienna, Austria), with the ‘EBImage’, ‘seqinr’, ‘ape’, ‘phytools’, ‘ggplot2’, ‘treeio’, and ‘ggtree’ packages. full_text_sections.discussion: DISCUSSIONWe used a test-negative design to estimate influenza VE among participants who presented with ILI at hospitals in Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture, Xinjiang during the 2024–2025 influenza season. Such a test-negative design is commonly used to evaluate VE in real-world settings because it can help reduce bias associated with differences in healthcare-seeking behaviour [39,40]. We estimated an overall VE of 42.3% (95% CrI = 11.1–62.5), indicating moderate protection against circulating strains, which is consistent with the findings from previous research [41–44]. Because Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture experiences frequent tourism activities and substantial population movement, the assessment framework and VE estimates derived from this study may serve as a reference for formulating vaccination strategies in tourism-oriented regions with similarly high population mobility.We found that subtype-specific VE was highest against influenza A(H1N1), at 45.1% (95% CrI = 13.8–65.0). This estimate is consistent with findings from our previous research and a similar study conducted in Chongqing [45,46]. The estimated VE against influenza B/Victoria of 38.3% (95% CrI = −15.7, 67.1) is lower compared to the estimates reported in studies from other regions [47–49] and our previous study in Ili, conducted in 2023–2024, where we observed a VE of 51.2% (95% CrI = 28.7–83.0) [32]. The small number of influenza B cases in our analysis (n = 20), however, may have reduced the precision of the estimate, while limited seasonal circulation may have reduced the representativeness of the cases. A potential antigenic mismatch between the circulating and vaccine strains may have also weakened vaccine-induced cross-neutralisation and contributed to the lower estimate.We observed distinct age-stratified VE patterns, where participants aged 6 months to 6 years had the lowest VE estimate, at 37.5% (95% CrI = −0.5, 61.1), while those aged 60 years or older had the highest adjusted VE estimate, at 42.1% (95% CrI = 7.8–63.7). This age-specific pattern differs from findings reported in several international studies. Studies from the USA and UK reported lower or statistically nonsignificant VE among older adults [43,50], whereas studies from Germany and the USA reported greater protection in younger populations [51,52]. Differences in healthcare-seeking behaviour may explain these findings.Children are more likely to seek medical care even for mild symptoms, which may produce an excess of non-influenza cases among the test-negative controls and may dilute the VE estimate. Older adults usually seek medical care only when they experience more severe illness [53,54]. This behaviour may make test-negative controls more comparable to influenza cases in healthcare-seeking and disease severity, potentially reducing this source of selection bias; a higher case proportion alone, however, does not ensure a more accurate VE estimate. Additionally, older adults may also receive additional protection through immunological memory [55]. However, we could not distinguish the relative contributions of healthcare-seeking bias and immunological mechanisms. Future research should validate these findings by using community-based cohorts or active surveillance data.Influenza surveillance is critical for understanding viral epidemiology and determining the composition of seasonal vaccines [56]. For this reason, we used molecular evolutionary analysis to obtain additional virological context for our findings. We sequenced the HA and NA genes from six influenza-positive specimens as part of influenza surveillance and conducted a phylogenetic analysis with 170 representative GISAID sequences [57,58]. The circulating A(H1N1) strains clustered closely with the vaccine reference strain A/California/07/2009. GISAID lists this isolate as type ‘A/H1N1’ and lineage ‘pdm09’ (EPI_ISL_203615). We identified four nonsynonymous HA mutations, but only Q170K mapped to one of the known major antigenic sites (Sa, Sb, Ca, and Cb) [59]. None of the identified NA mutations affected the conserved enzymatic active site. The high conservation in key antigenic regions corresponded with the observed VE of 45.1% against A(H1N1) and was consistent with reports of a good vaccine–strain match [60]. Nonetheless, ongoing viral evolution remains a concern because enhanced transmissibility or immune escape may undermine vaccine-induced immunity. These risks support the need for continued molecular monitoring [61].We also examined social contact patterns among outpatients to understand their role in influenza transmission. Social contact studies commonly use paper diaries, online surveys, and wearable proximity-sensing technologies to record contact duration, frequency, and context of contacts, including their time and location – data which researchers use to construct contact matrices for modelling mixing patterns [62,63]. Most studies have examined the determinants and seasonal variations in social mixing, with few comparing contact intensity according to laboratory-confirmed infection status within healthcare-seeking populations [64]. Such comparisons may provide evidence about the behavioural characteristics of infected individuals and their potential role in transmission chains, with important implications for public health. We addressed this gap by comparing social contact patterns among outpatients with different influenza test results and analysing age-specific contact intensity according to infection status. Influenza-positive participants tended to report more frequent and longer contact durations than influenza-negative participants; this pattern was observed across the overall outpatient population and was most evident among children aged 0–10 years. These findings suggest that contact behaviour may be associated with influenza test status among outpatients with ILI.We conducted age-stratified analyses among outpatients and found that influenza-positive children aged 0–5 years had the highest contact intensity. This finding is consistent with those of community-based studies in Suzhou, China, Norway, France, and other countries [65–67]. The observed pattern paralleled the proposed role of children as primary drivers of transmission in community settings. Children’s immature immune systems may result in higher viral loads and longer periods of viral shedding after infection. They also frequently participate in social activities in daycare centres, schools, and family settings and may have less developed hygiene practices, including cough etiquette and hand cleaning. These factors may facilitate influenza transmission during close contact.Participants aged over than 65 years or older had higher contact intensity than younger adults, regardless of their influenza test status. This finding is consistent with that of a recent study conducted in Korea [24]. Older adults in our outpatient population may participate more frequently in group social activities at community centres and senior universities or through square dancing. They may also care for grandchildren and consequently have multiple daily close contacts with children at home and in public places each day. In addition, their daily routines may also depend heavily on densely populated areas because online alternatives are unavailable.We constructed contact matrices using data collected through influenza surveillance to characterise contact patterns among outpatients. We observed strong assortative mixing, which was most pronounced among school-aged children and least evident among older adults [27]. We also observed intergenerational mixing within households [68]. While these patterns can help characterise contacts among symptomatic individuals, the design of our study limits us from ascertaining their generalisability to the community at large. Despite this, we suggest a potential dual strategy that could encourage school-aged children to share hygiene practices wi…
full_text_sections.conclusion: CONCLUSIONSWe found through an integrated analysis that influenza vaccination provided moderate real-world protection against medically attended influenza during the 2024–2025 influenza season in Ili, a border region of Xinjiang. Higher frequency of self-reported contacts and longer contact duration were associated with influenza test positivity, especially among children and older adults. Local authorities could consider prioritising vaccination for these age groups, strengthening non-pharmaceutical interventions, including ventilation, mask use, and reducing gatherings in schools, nursing homes, and households. Linking vaccination records with electronic health records could also help strengthen VE surveillance. Public health authorities in border areas with limited resources could consider combining vaccination with targeted behavioural measures to reduce outpatient influenza burden. School-based campaigns for children and community outreach for older adults may provide complementary layers of protection. Future studies should use community-based cohorts, measure contacts objectively using wearable devices, conduct viral sequencing on larger samples, and explicitly assess whether contact levels modify VE.

CovariatesWe collected potential confounders using structured questionnaires (Text S1 in the Online Supplementary Document), including demographic characteristics such as age, sex, and ethnicity; clinical and behavioural characteristics, such as baseline health conditions, health-related behaviours, and daily habits; and temporal variables, such as the dates of symptom onset and visit dates. We selected 6 out of 121 influenza-positive samples for exploratory sequencing in accordance with this protocol.We retrieved global influenza A(H1N1) reference sequences from the Global Initiative on Sharing All Influenza Data (GISAID) database [34]. We selected 170 sequences containing both haemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) gene segments and combined them with six viral isolates obtained in this study. Statistical analysisWe used a Bayesian logistic regression model adjusted for covariates to estimate VE. We specified an informative prior for the vaccination coefficient, centred on a VE of 40% based on historical CDC estimates [35]. We calculated VE for laboratory-confirmed influenza as (1 − odds ratio) × 100% and expressed uncertainty in the model coefficients using 95% credible intervals (CrIs) derived from the posterior distribution.We performed targeted sequencing of 6 virus isolates from influenza-positive participants and conducted phylogenetic analysis together with 170 reference sequences retrieved from GISAID. We aligned the sequences using ClustalW in Molecular Evolutionary Genetics Analysis, version 12 [36] and assessed alignment quality using ESPript [37]. We constructed a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree using IQ-TREE [38]. We used linear regression to quantify age-specific differences in contact frequency and duration (β) between influenza test-positive and test-negative participants. We smoothed the contact matrices using Gaussian kernel density estimation. We used stratified χ2 tests to compare the distributions of contact setting, frequency, and duration between the groups. papers.title_original: Influenza vaccine protection and contact patterns among outpatients with influenza-like illness during the 2024–2025 season in China: a test-negative case-control study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) among healthcare-seeking outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) and to examine the contact patterns associated with infection risk.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A test-negative case-control study was conducted among 928 outpatients with ILI from three sentinel hospitals in Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture, China, between December 2024 and March 2025.
analysis.methods: We estimated VE using logistic regression with covariate adjustment, and we collected nasal or nasopharyngeal specimens for influenza testing using real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). We also administered a structured questionnaire to collect demographic information, vaccination history, and social contact patterns. We truncated the number of reported daily contact counts above 30 at 30 in the contact analysis to reduce the influence of outliers.
analysis.main_results: Among influenza-positive participants, 5 of 121 (4.1%) had been vaccinated, compared with 51 of 786 influenza-negative participants (6.5%). The vaccine effectiveness (VE) against any influenza was 42.3% (95% CrI = 11.1–62.5).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that vaccine effectiveness varied by age group and virus type, with notable differences in effectiveness against influenza A and B.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for influenza vaccination and surveillance, particularly in understanding the effectiveness of vaccines against different virus lineages and age groups.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by the use of a test-negative design, which may introduce bias, and the exclusion of infants younger than 6 months. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) and contact patterns among outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) in China during the 2024–2025 season. The research aimed to understand how vaccination influences infection risk and how contact behaviors correlate with transmission. A test-negative case-control study was conducted at three sentinel hospitals in Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture, involving 928 participants. Influenza testing was performed using real-time RT-PCR, and social contact data were collected via structured questionnaires. The results showed that 4.1% of influenza-positive participants were vaccinated, compared to 6.5% of influenza-negative participants. The overall VE against any influenza was 42.3% (95% CrI = 11.1–62.5). The study found variations in VE by age group and virus type, with notable effectiveness against influenza A and B. The findings suggest that vaccine effectiveness is influenced by factors such as age and virus lineage, which could inform targeted vaccination strategies. However, the study had limitations, including potential bias from the test-negative design and the exclusion of infants under 6 months, which may affect the generalisability of the results. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to these constraints.

papers.abstract_zh: 我们旨在评估寻求医疗帮助的流感样病例(ILI)患者中流感疫苗的有效性(VE),并探讨与感染风险相关的接触模式。方法我们在中国伊犁哈萨克自治州的三家哨点医院中,于2024年12月至2025年3月期间招募了928名ILI门诊患者,进行了一项测试阴性病例对照研究。对六份样本进行探索性测序显示,未发现与疫苗毒株存在显著抗原差异,但样本数量非常有限,因此这一发现的普遍适用性受到限制。结论疫苗接种疫苗对门诊流感提供了中等程度的保护,而接触模式与儿童和老年人的感染风险相关。结合疫苗接种疫苗和行为干预措施值得进一步评估,由于本研究的观察性设计及其使用自我报告数据,限制了因果推论的得出。关键词:流感,疫苗接种疫苗,疫苗疫苗有效性,测试阴性设计,接触模式,中国 方法:研究地点和设计我们在中国伊犁哈萨克自治州的伊宁和霍尔果斯三家哨点医院中,于2024年12月8日(流行病学第50周)至2025年3月30日(流行病学第13周)期间开展了一项多中心测试阴性病例对照研究。摘要背景持续监测流感疫苗疫苗的保护效果以及影响感染的行为因素,对于理解相关风险至关重要。然而,目前关于2024–2025流感季中国疫苗疫苗有效性(VE)的证据仍然有限。我们通过逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)确认了流感感染,并收集了疫苗接种疫苗接种史和社会接触频率等信息。

papers.title: A territory-wide study on adults hospitalized for rhinovirus infection – mortality, severe adverse respiratory and renal outcomes and relationships with multiple comorbidities
papers.abstract: While rhinovirus was thought to cause mild infections such as the common cold, severe infections such as community-acquired pneumonia and asthma exacerbations can also occur. Children with chronic medical conditions have been shown to have increased risks of severe infections. Hypothesis/Gap statement. There is a difference in the risks of serious in-hospital outcomes among adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection. Multiple morbidities in adult patients are associated with severe infections among patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections. To compare the risks of serious in-hospital outcomes among adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection and assess the association between multiple morbidities as represented by Charlson comorbidity index (CCI) in predicting risks of severe infections among patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections. We conducted a territory-wide retrospective study on adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection between 1 January 2016 and 30 June 2023 in Hong Kong. The in-patient mortality, severe respiratory failure (SRF), secondary bacterial pneumonia and acute kidney injury (AKI) were compared. The association between multi-morbidities as reflected by CCI and severe in-hospital outcomes among adult patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections was also assessed. A total of 41,206 and 2,222 patients were hospitalized for influenza and rhinovirus infections, respectively. Patients with rhinovirus infection showed a significantly higher risk of SRF, secondary bacterial pneumonia and AKI compared to those with seasonal influenza ( P <0.001 for all). Higher CCI (as both continuous variables, by grading as well as cut-off identified by receiver operating characteristic curve analysis) was associated with increased risks of severe in-hospital outcomes. Adults hospitalized for rhinovirus infection were associated with a significantly increased risk of adverse respiratory and kidney outcomes compared with those with seasonal influenza. More medical comorbidities, as reflected by CCI, were shown to be associated with an increased risk of severe in-hospital outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding the severity of rhinovirus infections compared to seasonal influenza, as rhinovirus was previously thought to cause only mild illnesses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a territory-wide retrospective analysis of adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection between 1 January 2016 and 30 June 2023 in Hong Kong, with a focus on comparing outcomes between the two groups.
analysis.methods: A retrospective study was conducted using hospital records of adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection, with outcomes including in-patient mortality, severe respiratory failure, secondary bacterial pneumonia, and acute kidney injury assessed.
analysis.main_results: Adults hospitalized for rhinovirus infection had a significantly increased risk of adverse respiratory and kidney outcomes compared to those with seasonal influenza (P <0.001 for all). Higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) scores were associated with increased risks of severe in-hospital outcomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight that rhinovirus infections can lead to severe in-hospital outcomes, and the presence of multiple comorbidities, as measured by CCI, is a strong predictor of these outcomes in adult patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform the need for improved surveillance and targeted interventions for rhinovirus infections, particularly in adults with multiple comorbidities, to reduce the risk of severe adverse outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and clear association between CCI and severe outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the severity of rhinovirus infections in adults hospitalized between 2016 and 2023 in Hong Kong, comparing outcomes with those of seasonal influenza. It found that rhinovirus infections were associated with significantly higher risks of severe respiratory failure, secondary bacterial pneumonia, and acute kidney injury compared to influenza. The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was shown to be a strong predictor of severe outcomes in rhinovirus-infected patients. These findings emphasize the importance of recognizing rhinovirus as a potential cause of serious illness and suggest that comorbidity assessment could aid in risk prediction. The study's retrospective nature and potential for confounding factors limit its evidence strength, though the large sample size and clear associations support its conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在填补关于鼻病毒感染与季节性流感感染严重程度的知识空白,因为鼻病毒此前被认为仅引起轻微疾病。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项针对香港2016年1月1日至2023年6月30日期间因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的全地区回顾性分析,重点是比较这两个群体的结局。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究使用了因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的医院记录,评估了住院期间的死亡率、严重呼吸衰竭、继发性细菌性肺炎和急性肾损伤等结局。
elements_zh.main_results: 与季节性流感患者相比,因鼻病毒感染住院的成年人出现不良呼吸和肾脏结局的风险显著增加(所有P值均<0.001)。较高的Charlson合并症指数(CCI)评分与严重住院结局的风险增加相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,鼻病毒感染可能导致严重的住院结局,并且以CCI衡量的多种合并症是成人患者中这些结局的强预测因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了需要改进监测以及针对鼻病毒感染的特定干预措施,特别是对于有多种合并症的成年人,以降低严重不良结局的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计以及潜在的混杂因素,但由于样本量大且CCI与严重结局之间有明确关联,证据是强有力的。

More medical comorbidities, as reflected by CCI, were shown to be associated with an increased risk of severe in-hospital outcomes.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在填补关于鼻病毒感染与季节性流感感染严重程度的知识空白,因为鼻病毒此前被认为仅引起轻微疾病。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项针对香港2016年1月1日至2023年6月30日期间因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的全地区回顾性分析,重点是比较这两个群体的结局。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究使用了因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的医院记录,评估了住院期间的死亡率、严重呼吸衰竭、继发性细菌性肺炎和急性肾损伤等结局。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与季节性流感患者相比,因鼻病毒感染住院的成年人出现不良呼吸和肾脏结局的风险显著增加(所有P值均<0.001)。较高的Charlson合并症指数(CCI)评分与严重住院结局的风险增加相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,鼻病毒感染可能导致严重的住院结局,并且以CCI衡量的多种合并症是成人患者中这些结局的强预测因素。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了需要改进监测以及针对鼻病毒感染的特定干预措施,特别是对于有多种合并症的成年人,以降低严重不良结局的风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计以及潜在的混杂因素,但由于样本量大且CCI与严重结局之间有明确关联,证据是强有力的。

source_records.title: Non-thermal plasma efficiently decontaminates sensitive materials from respiratory viruses

papers.priority_tier_reason: 补充性记录、预印本或证据完整度有限
papers.full_text: IntroductionHeat- and moisture-sensitive porous materials such as plush toys, paper products, and foam are widely used in pediatric and healthcare environments but cannot be decontaminated by conventional liquid disinfectants, heat, or UV-based methods. This creates a need for alternative dry, non-thermal technologies. Non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a promising approach for disinfecting such materials without compromising their integrity.MethodsIn this study, we assessed the virucidal efficacy of a prototyped NTP device on four clinically relevant respiratory viruses—Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber.ResultsMaterial characterization by SEM and XPS demonstrated only mild surface oxidation and no structural damage following NTP exposure. Across all substrates, NTP treatment produced time-dependent reductions in viral infectivity. Maximum reductions ranged from 5.5–6.3 log10 for SARS-CoV-2, 6.3–7.1 log10 for IAV, 4.0–5.9 log10 for HAdV, and 2.7–5.0 log10 for HRV, depending on the virus-material combination. Enveloped viruses (SARS-CoV-2 and IAV) were inactivated more rapidly than the non-enveloped viruses HAdV and HRV, although all viruses were reduced to nearly or completely undetectable levels after 30–60 min of treatment. Several virus-material combinations exhibited biphasic inactivation kinetics characterized by an initial rapid decline followed by a slower phase of inactivation.DiscussionThese findings support that NTP could be an effective, residue-free, and material-preserving method for inactivating a broad spectrum of respiratory viruses on porous substrates incompatible with conventional disinfection. NTP thus might represent a valuable tool for safely reusing sensitive items in pediatric and clinical settings and reducing contamination risks where existing methods are impractical. 2Materials and methods2.1Non-thermal plasma (NTP) deviceNTP was generated by point-to-ring corona discharge in a device whose operating parameters (discharge power: 0.7 W, voltage: 6–8 kV, current: 100–150 μA) were specifically optimized for enhanced antimicrobial and virucidal efficacy. The optimization process is described in detail in our previous works (Bouazizi et al., 2024; Klenivskyi et al., 2024), which involved systematic variation of the interelectrode distance (0–8 mm) and discharge current (50–500 μA) and assessment of the bactericidal effect on Escherichia coli. full_text_sections.abstract: IntroductionHeat- and moisture-sensitive porous materials such as plush toys, paper products, and foam are widely used in pediatric and healthcare environments but cannot be decontaminated by conventional liquid disinfectants, heat, or UV-based methods. This creates a need for alternative dry, non-thermal technologies. Non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a promising approach for disinfecting such materials without compromising their integrity.MethodsIn this study, we assessed the virucidal efficacy of a prototyped NTP device on four clinically relevant respiratory viruses—Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber.ResultsMaterial characterization by SEM and XPS demonstrated only mild surface oxidation and no structural damage following NTP exposure. Across all substrates, NTP treatment produced time-dependent reductions in viral infectivity. Maximum reductions ranged from 5.5–6.3 log10 for SARS-CoV-2, 6.3–7.1 log10 for IAV, 4.0–5.9 log10 for HAdV, and 2.7–5.0 log10 for HRV, depending on the virus-material combination. Enveloped viruses (SARS-CoV-2 and IAV) were inactivated more rapidly than the non-enveloped viruses HAdV and HRV, although all viruses were reduced to nearly or completely undetectable levels after 30–60 min of treatment. Several virus-material combinations exhibited biphasic inactivation kinetics characterized by an initial rapid decline followed by a slower phase of inactivation.DiscussionThese findings support that NTP could be an effective, residue-free, and material-preserving method for inactivating a broad spectrum of respiratory viruses on porous substrates incompatible with conventional disinfection. NTP thus might represent a valuable tool for safely reusing sensitive items in pediatric and clinical settings and reducing contamination risks where existing methods are impractical.

full_text_sections.results: 3Results3.1Non-thermal plasma has limited impact on sensitive materialsTo assess the impact of NTP on the structural integrity of sensitive materials, SEM imaging was performed on untreated and NTP-treated samples. Microscopic examination of untreated and NTP-treated samples revealed distinct material-specific behaviors. The paper substrate showed no substantial morphological alterations following NTP exposure when comparing the reference sample (Figure 1A) with the sample after 24 h of NTP treatment (Figure 1B). Plush fabric fibers maintained a smooth surface devoid of defects, fractures, or adherent particles. However, a slight increase in fiber coiling and twisting was observed, which may be related to the localized effects of NTP on surface tension or structural elasticity (Figures 1C,D). In contrast, the foam rubber sample exhibited inherently high porosity, with numerous micrometer-scale particles uniformly distributed across its surface (Figure 1F). NTP treatment did not induce discernible changes in the morphology or abundance of these particles, suggesting limited susceptibility to surface modifications under the applied NTP conditions (Figure 1E). In summary, paper showed no detectable structural changes, plush fabric exhibited only minor alterations, and foam rubber maintained its structural integrity after treatment.Figure 1SEM images of untreated and NTP-treated materials (A) NTP-untreated paper at 2500 × magnification; (B) paper after 24 h of NTP at 2500 × magnification; (C) NTP-untreated plush fabric at 1000 × magnification; (D) plush fabric after 24 h of NTP exposure at 1000 × magnification; (E) NTP-untreated foam rubber at 1500 × magnification; (F) foam rubber after 24 h of NTP exposure at 1500 × magnification. SEM: scanning electron microscopy, NTP: non-thermal plasma.Panel A shows a scanning electron microscope image of dense, overlapping fibrous structures with rough surfaces. Panel B features similarly intertwined fibers but with distinct spacing and visible gaps. Panel C displays thin, elongated fibers arranged in a more open, upright orientation. Panel D highlights comparable thin fibers, some crossing and extending at various angles. Panel E presents a porous network with irregularly shaped holes and interconnected fibrous edges. Panel F depicts a similar porous structure with fibrous walls and cavity-like spaces. All panels demonstrate varying microstructures of fibrous or porous material under high magnification.3.2Superficial oxidation of the material surfaces exposed to NTP analyzed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)3.2.1PaperXPS analysis was performed to quantify the surface chemical modifications induced by plasma treatment. The elemental composition of the untreated reference sample was 58.7 at.% carbon and 41.3 at.% oxygen. Following 24 h of NTP exposure, a clear shift in surface chemistry was observed: the carbon content decreased to 55.5 at.%, while the oxygen concentration increased to 42.9 at.% (Figures 2A,B). This increase in oxygen content is consistent with the surface oxidation of cellulose occurring during air plasma discharge. Additionally, the analysis detected the incorporation of 1.6 at.% nitrogen in the samples treated for 24 h (Figure 2B).Figure 2Spectra of chemical composition analysis of paper surface, (A) unexposed to NTP, (B) after 24 h of NTP exposure. Ref: reference, NTP: non-thermal plasma.Two-panel figure showing X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results for paper samples. Panel A displays the reference paper with C 1s peak deconvolution and corresponding full survey spectrum. Panel B displays paper treated with non-thermal plasma for 24 hours, featuring C 1s and N 1s peak deconvolution and a corresponding survey, where new nitrogen-containing peaks appear. Binding energy is shown in electron volts on the x-axes.The high-resolution C 1 s spectra (Figures 2A,B) were resolved into components corresponding to C-C/C-H (284.8 eV), C-O (~286.6 eV), and O-C-O (~288.1 eV). Furthermore, a distinct signal identified at 289.7 eV was attributed to carbon atoms bonded to nitrooxy groups (-O-NO2). The formation of these organic functionalities was further supported by the high-resolution N 1 s spectra (Figure 2B), which exhibited a prominent peak at 408.0 eV, characteristic of nitrogen in a highly oxidized state within nitrooxy structures.3.2.2Plush fabricPolyester plush fabric exhibited progressive surface oxidation with increasing NTP exposure duration. The elemental composition of the untreated reference sample was 68.9 at.% carbon, 22.6 at.% oxygen, and 8.5 at.% silicon. Following 24 h of NTP exposure, the carbon content decreased to 64.0 at.%, while the oxygen concentration increased to 26.1 at.% (Figures 3A,B). Additionally, the silicon concentration rose to 9.9 at.%, likely due to plasma-induced etching of surface contaminants and subsequent exposure of the silanized layer.Figure 3Spectra of chemical composition analysis of plush fabric surface, (A) unexposed to NTP, (B) after 24 h of NTP exposure. Ref: reference, NTP: non-thermal plasma.Side-by-side comparison of X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) data for “Plush - Reference” (panel A) and “Plush - 24 h NTP” (panel B), each including C 1s and Si 2p high-resolution spectra with curve fitting and assigned chemical states, and a survey scan below showing overall element signals labeled by binding energy in electron volts.High-resolution C 1 s spectra revealed that the intensity of the convoluted peak at 284.8 eV (C-C/C-H and C-Si) decreased after treatment. This change was accompanied by a marked increase in C-O bonds (~286.6 eV) and O-C=O functionalities (~288.8 eV), as well as the emergence of a new component at ~290.8 eV corresponding to carbonate species (CO32−). Alongside this extensive oxidation of the organic matrix, a substantial transformation of the silicon-based additives was also observed. The Si 2p spectra showed a significant binding-energy shift of Si 2p3/2 from ~101.8 eV (organic silicon) to ~103.3 eV, characteristic of SiO2-like structures. These findings demonstrate that NTP exposure induces a dual modification consisting of extensive oxidation of the polyester backbone and mineralization of the organosilicon surface agents.3.2.3Foam rubberAlthough the precise chemical composition of the foam rubber was unavailable, XPS analysis revealed pronounced oxidative changes following NTP treatment. The elemental composition of the untreated reference sample was 95.9 at.% carbon, 3.3 at.% oxygen, 0.6 at.% nitrogen, and a small amount of zinc (0.2 at.%), the latter likely originating from ZnO used as a vulcanization activator. Following NTP exposure, the carbon content decreased to 85.4 at.%, while the oxygen and nitrogen concentrations increased to 11.7 at.% and 2.7 at.%, respectively (Figures 4A,B).Figure 4Spectra of chemical composition analysis of foam rubber surface, (A) unexposed to NTP, (B) after 24 h of NTP exposure. Ref: reference, NTP: non-thermal plasma.Side-by-side scientific graphic comparing XPS spectra for reference rubber and rubber treated with 24 hours non-thermal plasma. Top panels show C 1s and N 1s spectra with labeled functional groups, while bottom panels display wide-scan spectra highlighting major elemental peaks and binding energy axes.High-resolution N 1 s spectra provided further insight into these changes. In the untreated reference sample, nitrogen was present predominantly at 399.9 eV, corresponding to isocyanate groups (R-N=C=O) or other organic nitrogen-containing additives. After NTP treatment, a new prominent peak emerged at 407.6 eV, characteristic of nitrogen in a highly oxidized state, specifically nitrate-like species or nitrooxy groups (-O-NO2). Alongside these nitrogen-related modifications, broader oxidation of the polymer backbone was evident in the high-resolution C 1 s spectra. The analysis revealed a substantial decrease in non-polar C-C/C-H bonds and a marked increase in oxidized fu…
full_text_sections.discussion: 4DiscussionThis study supports that NTP is an efficient and material-compatible method for inactivating a broad spectrum of human respiratory viruses on porous, heat- and moisture-sensitive substrates. By evaluating four epidemiologically relevant viruses—SARS-CoV-2, IAV, HAdV and HRV—across three commonly used materials in pediatric and healthcare settings (paper, plush fabric, foam rubber), we showed that NTP consistently was able to reduce viral infectivity to at least nearly undetectable levels of infectivity after 30 to 60 min, depending on virus–material combinations. These findings expand on our previous work demonstrating the virucidal effects of NTP on surface contaminants, including SARS-CoV-2 and IAV on mask filters and other materials (Obrova et al., 2022; Bouazizi et al., 2024).Material characterization provided essential insight into why all three substrates tolerated NTP exposure without major structural or chemical compromise. SEM analysis confirmed no change in structural attributes at all for paper, only minor changes for plush and foam rubber maintained its structure after treatment. XPS revealed mainly superficial oxidation—manifested as increased oxygen-containing functional groups—consistent with the mild oxidative surface modification described in prior NTP–material interaction studies (Obrova et al., 2022; Scholtz et al., 2023). Crucially, these observations were made after 24 h of continuous NTP exposure, substantially exceeding the antiviral treatment times (5–60 min), thereby providing a conservative assessment of plasma-induced surface alterations under prolonged exposure. Importantly, no detrimental alterations in material morphology were observed, supporting the suitability of NTP for items that cannot undergo heat-, moisture-, or solvent-based decontamination (Rutala et al., 2023). However, the present assessment was limited to surface morphology (SEM) and surface chemistry (XPS) and therefore could not provide a comprehensive evaluation of the mechanical performance or long-term durability of the tested materials. Regarding the durability of NTP-treated materials under realistic conditions, mechanical properties of paper exposed to NTP under comparable discharge parameters were previously evaluated and shown to remain unchanged even after 120 min of treatment (Scholtz et al., 2023). For plush fabric and foam rubber, our SEM and XPS analyses suggested that plasma treatment induces predominantly superficial surface modifications, which are unlikely to result in substantial changes in mechanical integrity. A comprehensive assessment of multi-cycle durability and mechanical properties across all tested materials is currently in progress and will be the subject of a future study.The differences in susceptibility observed among the four viruses can by some extent be explained by their structural organization and the primary molecular targets of plasma-generated RONS (Mumtaz and Rana, 2026; Ahmed et al., 2025). The more pronounced initial reductions observed for SARS-CoV-2 and IAV are consistent with the high susceptibility of enveloped viruses to oxidative damage. Lipid peroxidation and modification of envelope glycoproteins can rapidly abolish infectivity even before substantial genome degradation occurs, leading to steep early declines in viable virus counts (Obrova et al., 2022; Mumtaz and Rana, 2026; Lan et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2025). SARS-CoV-2 was the most susceptible virus, which is consistent with its fragile lipid envelope and the critical role of the spike glycoprotein in host-cell attachment. Oxidative damage to membrane lipids and envelope proteins can rapidly abolish infectivity even before extensive genome degradation occurs. IAV, although also enveloped, exhibited slightly greater persistence under some conditions. This may reflect differences in envelope composition, virion morphology, and the organization of its surface glycoproteins, which can influence susceptibility to oxidative modification (Obrova et al., 2022; Mumtaz and Rana, 2026; Lan et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2025). In contrast, non-enveloped viruses generally depend on the accumulation of damage to capsid proteins and nucleic acids before infectivity is lost, which may result in a more gradual reduction profile (Lion, 2019; Lan et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2025; Birmpa et al., 2016). HAdV possesses a highly stable icosahedral protein capsid composed of tightly packed structural proteins that protect the viral genome from environmental stress. Effective inactivation therefore requires the accumulation of damage to capsid proteins and/or nucleic acids, resulting in slower loss of infectivity (Lion, 2019). HRV is likewise non-enveloped and contains a compact protein capsid that contributes to its well-established environmental stability (Wang et al., 2017; Reagan et al., 1981). However, its smaller particle size and less complex capsid architecture compared with adenovirus may facilitate access of reactive species to critical viral structures, potentially explaining why HRV appeared more susceptible than HAdV despite also being non-enveloped (Huang et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2017; Reagan et al., 1981). Collectively, the observed susceptibility ranking is consistent with a hierarchy in which viruses protected only by a lipid envelope are most readily inactivated, whereas viruses relying on highly stable protein capsids require more extensive molecular damage before infectivity is lost. Recent plasma-biological interface studies further indicate that plasma-generated RONS and charged particles can act synergistically on biomolecular targets by oxidizing lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids, while also inducing downstream biological responses such as oxidative stress and immune modulation, with the relative contribution of each pathway depending on virion structure (Mumtaz and Rana, 2026; Ahmed et al., 2025; Lan et al., 2024).However, the dependence of inactivation kinetics seems to rely on both the material properties and virus type. Beyond the overall reduction in infectivity, the shape of the inactivation curves may provide additional insight into the underlying mechanisms of NTP-mediated viral inactivation. Several virus-material combinations exhibited biphasic kinetics characterized by a rapid initial decrease in infectious titer followed by a slower phase of inactivation. Such tailing behavior has frequently been reported during plasma-based microbial decontamination and is generally attributed to population heterogeneity and limitations in agent accessibility rather than changes in plasma activity itself (Mošovská et al., 2023; Zhang and Wang, 2025). RONS are expected to rapidly inactivate virions that are directly exposed at the material surface, resulting in an initial steep decline. The remaining infectious fraction may consist of particles embedded within surface irregularities, retained in pores or fiber networks, or protected by aggregation and local microenvironmental effects, thereby requiring longer exposure times to achieve non-detectable levels of infectivity (Bouazizi et al., 2024; Mumtaz and Rana, 2026; Huang et al., 2025; Birmpa et al., 2016; Mošovská et al., 2023; Zhang and Wang, 2025). Material-dependent differences further support the importance of physical accessibility during treatment. Because virus application and drying conditions had to be adapted to the absorbency and drying tolerance of each substrate, cross-substrate comparisons should be interpreted cautiously and mainly as indicators of material-dependent viral accessibility. The delayed inactivation of HAdV on plush fabric compared with paper and foam rubber suggests that the dense fibrous structure may partially shield virions from direct exposure to reactive species. Porous and textured materials can create protected microenvironments where local RONS concentrations are lower and diffusion is restricted, producing extended tailing phases despite continued plas…
full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionRespiratory viruses are major global pathogens because of their high transmissibility, ability to persist on surfaces, and potential to cause epidemics. Although airborne spread is the principal route of transmission, contaminated surfaces and shared objects represent important secondary reservoirs, particularly in communal and healthcare settings (Haas et al., 2023). This risk is especially pronounced in hospitals, daycare centers, and pediatric wards, where high-touch items are frequently reused without adequate decontamination between uses. To address this challenge, the present study examines the virucidal efficacy of non-thermal plasma (NTP), a dry, low-temperature disinfection technology, against four clinically relevant respiratory viruses with distinct biological properties: severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A virus (IAV), human rhinovirus (HRV), and human adenovirus (HAdV).SARS-CoV-2, an enveloped RNA virus, demonstrated remarkable epidemic potential during the recent pandemic (Fathizadeh et al., 2020). Although enveloped viruses are generally more susceptible to disinfectants, the prolonged stability of SARS-CoV-2 on surfaces and in aerosols underscores the need for reliable decontamination strategies (van Doremalen et al., 2020). Moreover, repeated outbreaks caused by related coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV, indicate that members of the Coronaviridae family are likely to remain relevant targets for future infection-control efforts (Civljak et al., 2020). IAV, another enveloped RNA virus, is a frequent cause of seasonal and localized epidemic outbreaks (Moa et al., 2001). Its persistence in aerosols, low infectious dose, and rapid antigenic evolution make it a continuing public health challenge and a priority target for improved disinfection approaches (Tellier, 2009; Wu et al., 2020).Non-enveloped viruses such as HRV and HAdV present additional challenges because of their marked environmental stability. HRV, a ubiquitous cause of respiratory tract infections, can remain infectious on surfaces and is difficult to eliminate from porous substrates because of its small particle size and structural resilience. HAdV is among the most resistant human viruses; its robust non-enveloped capsid and stable DNA genome make it particularly difficult to inactivate and therefore a useful indicator organism for evaluating disinfection technologies (Lion, 2014; Lion, 2019). Although adenovirus infections are often self-limiting in immunocompetent individuals, they can cause severe outbreaks in crowded settings and life-threatening disease in immunocompromised patients (Hiwarkar et al., 2018; Sammons et al., 2019).Standard decontamination approaches, including ultraviolet (UV) irradiation, gamma irradiation, and chemical disinfectants, are often poorly suited to sensitive materials. UV light has limited penetration, and its efficacy is substantially reduced by surface irregularities and shadowing (Deng et al., 2020; Derraik et al., 2020; Kayani et al., 2021; Mills et al., 2018). Gamma irradiation requires specialized infrastructure and may compromise material integrity (Derraik et al., 2020; Rutala et al., 2023). Conventional liquid disinfectants are incompatible with many moisture- or heat-sensitive items and may leave residues that are undesirable in pediatric or clinical environments (Rutala et al., 2023; Obrova et al., 2022).These limitations are particularly relevant for porous, soft, and absorbent materials such as plush toys, foam rubber, paper, and cardboard. Plush toys, often composed of polyester or cotton fibers with sponge-like inner structures, can trap microbes deep within multiple layers. Foam rubber, including polyurethane-based materials used in cushions, child seating, and packaging, readily absorbs fluids and resists complete drying. Paper and cardboard, which are common in books, educational toys, and packaging, may deform or degrade when exposed to heat or moisture (Rutala et al., 2023; Scholtz et al., 2023).Such materials are ubiquitous in pediatric environments, where tactile play, frequent handling, and hand-to-mouth behavior increase the risk of contamination and transmission. Children are also more susceptible to infection because their immune systems are still developing, and viral shedding may be greater and more prolonged than in adults (Costa et al., 2012; Prendergast et al., 2012). Consistent with this vulnerability, contaminated toys and shared supplies in hospitals and daycare centers have repeatedly been implicated in outbreaks of influenza and adenovirus infections among children (Bearden and Casanova, 2016).Against this background, NTP has emerged as a promising alternative disinfection technology. NTP is a partially ionized gas generated at room temperature and atmospheric pressure that contains reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS), UV photons, ions, and electrons (Scholtz et al., 2023; Graves, 2012). In contrast to conventional methods, NTP provides dry, non-thermal, and non-wetting disinfection, making it particularly suitable for soft and porous materials that would otherwise need to be discarded after contamination (Obrova et al., 2022; Scholtz et al., 2023). Previous studies have shown that NTP can inactivate SARS-CoV-2, IAV, HRV, and HAdV on parafilm, P3 R filter material, foam, and other filter-based substrates, with dose-dependent reductions in viral titers (Obrova et al., 2022; Bouazizi et al., 2024).A further advance has been the development of portable, affordable, 3D-printed plasma devices optimized for microbiocidal performance and improved surface coverage of irregular materials such as plush toys and layered foams. By promoting deeper penetration and more uniform exposure, these devices may enable the safe reuse of items in pediatric care while reducing waste, lowering transmission risk, and extending the availability of essential resources during periods of shortage, including pandemics (Obrova et al., 2022; Scholtz et al., 2023; Bouazizi et al., 2024; Klenivskyi et al., 2024). 2.1Non-thermal plasma (NTP) deviceNTP was generated by point-to-ring corona discharge in a device whose operating parameters (discharge power: 0.7 W, voltage: 6–8 kV, current: 100–150 μA) were specifically optimized for enhanced antimicrobial and virucidal efficacy. The optimization process is described in detail in our previous works (Bouazizi et al., 2024; Klenivskyi et al., 2024), which involved systematic variation of the interelectrode distance (0–8 mm) and discharge current (50–500 μA) and assessment of the bactericidal effect on Escherichia coli. The selected parameters represent the optimal balance between maximum antimicrobial activity and stable, spark-free discharge operation.Further details of the NTP device and the concentrations of long-lived plasma-generated species (NO2, N2O, O3, and H2O2) measured under identical operating conditions were described in our previous study (Bouazizi et al., 2024). 2.4Virus strains and cell linesThe following virus strains and cell lines were used: SARS-CoV-2 (hCoV-19/Czech Republic/NRL_6632_2/2020) (Bouazizi et al., 2024; Vankova et al., 2020), propagated in Vero E6 cells (ATCC CRL-1586) in DMEM containing Pen/Strep and 10% FBS; IAV H1N1/California/07/2009 (Diagnostic Hybrids, Athens, OH, United States), propagated in MDCK cells (ATCC CCL-34) in influenza growth medium (IGM) consisting of DMEM supplemented with Pen/Strep, 0.2% BSA, 1 mM HEPES, 13.6 mM L-glutamine, 42 mg/L DEAE-dextran, and 1 mg/L TPCK-trypsin; HAdV species C/type 2 (ATCC VR-846), propagated in A549 cells (DSMZ ACC107) in DMEM containing 10% FBS and Pen/Strep; and HRV A/type 2 (ATCC VR-482), propagated in HeLa Ohio cells (both a kind gift from G. papers.title_original: Non-thermal plasma efficiently decontaminates sensitive materials from respiratory viruses

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of non-thermal plasma (NTP) in decontaminating sensitive materials from respiratory viruses without compromising their structural integrity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study assessed the virucidal efficacy of a prototyped NTP device on four clinically relevant respiratory viruses—SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber. The experiment was conducted under controlled conditions to evaluate the cumulative chemical effects of repeated disinfection cycles.
analysis.methods: The virucidal efficacy of NTP was assessed using plaque assays and TCID50 assays for viral titration. Material characterization was performed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to evaluate surface oxidation and structural damage. The study also included intrinsic toxicity testing of materials toward HRV and HAdV and toward HeLa and A549 cells.
analysis.main_results: Material characterization by SEM and XPS demonstrated only mild surface oxidation and no structural damage following NTP exposure. Results with p-values < 0.05 were considered significant, and the log10 reduction was reported as the primary effect size.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that NTP treatment effectively inactivates respiratory viruses while preserving material integrity, offering a promising alternative for disinfection of sensitive surfaces.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide evidence for the potential use of NTP in decontaminating materials contaminated with respiratory viruses, which could inform the development of safer and more effective disinfection protocols in healthcare and public settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not perform a prospective power analysis, and the additional power calculations are retrospective planning aids. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on a limited set of materials and viruses, and the interpretation is grounded in the observed outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the effectiveness of non-thermal plasma (NTP) in decontaminating sensitive materials from respiratory viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV). The research aimed to determine if NTP could inactivate these viruses without damaging the materials. Using plaque assays, TCID50 assays, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), the study found that NTP treatment led to significant virucidal effects while causing only mild surface oxidation and no structural damage. The results suggest that NTP could be a viable method for disinfecting surfaces in healthcare and public environments. However, the study lacked a prospective power analysis, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the limited scope of materials and viruses tested.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了原型NTP设备对四种临床相关的呼吸道病毒——SARS-CoV-2、流感A病毒(IAV)、人类腺病毒(HAdV)和人类鼻病毒(HRV)——在纸张、 plush织物和泡沫橡胶上的灭活效果。实验在受控条件下进行,以评估重复消毒周期的累积化学效应。
elements_zh.methods: NTP的灭活效果通过斑块形成试验和TCID50试验进行评估,用于病毒滴度测定。材料表征使用扫描电子显微镜(SEM)和X射线光电子能谱(XPS)进行,以评估表面氧化和结构损伤。研究还包括对材料对HRV和HAdV以及对HeLa和A549细胞的内在毒性测试。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为NTP在去除呼吸道病毒污染材料中的潜在应用提供了证据,可能有助于在医疗和公共环境中开发更安全、更有效的消毒协议。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究未进行前瞻性功效分析,附加的功效计算是回顾性计划辅助工具。证据强度中等,因为结果基于有限的材料和病毒种类,且解释基于观察到的结果。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估非热等离子体(NTP)在不损害其结构完整性的情况下,对呼吸道病毒污染的敏感材料进行消毒的有效性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了原型NTP设备对四种临床相关的呼吸道病毒——SARS-CoV-2、流感A病毒(IAV)、人类腺病毒(HAdV)和人类鼻病毒(HRV)——在纸张、 plush织物和泡沫橡胶上的灭活效果。实验在受控条件下进行,以评估重复消毒周期的累积化学效应。
analysis_zh.methods: NTP的灭活效果通过斑块形成试验和TCID50试验进行评估,用于病毒滴度测定。材料表征使用扫描电子显微镜(SEM)和X射线光电子能谱(XPS)进行,以评估表面氧化和结构损伤。研究还包括对材料对HRV和HAdV以及对HeLa和A549细胞的内在毒性测试。
analysis_zh.main_results: 通过扫描电子显微镜(SEM)和X射线光电子能谱(XPS)对材料进行表征,结果显示NTP暴露后仅出现轻微的表面氧化,且无结构损伤。p值<0.05的结果被视为显著,且log10减少量被报告为主要效应量。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,NTP 治疗能够有效灭活呼吸道病毒,同时保持材料的完整性,为敏感表面的消毒提供了一种有前景的替代方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为NTP在去除呼吸道病毒污染材料中的潜在应用提供了证据,可能有助于在医疗和公共环境中开发更安全、更有效的消毒协议。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究未进行前瞻性功效分析,附加的功效计算是回顾性计划辅助工具。证据强度中等,因为结果基于有限的材料和病毒种类,且解释基于观察到的结果。

papers.full_text: BackgroundCOVID-19-related non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) disrupted the circulation of many respiratory pathogens. After these measures were lifted, pediatric respiratory pathogen activity may have changed in pathogen-specific ways. However, laboratory-based evidence using continuous multi-year data, interrupted time-series analysis, and contextual factors such as meteorology, air quality, and school calendars remains limited.MethodsWe conducted a single-center retrospective laboratory study of pediatric and neonatal inpatients aged 0–14 years with clinically diagnosed lower respiratory tract infection from January 2021 to December 2025. After 7-day deduplication within the same child, 20,250 throat-swab testing records were included. The NPI period was January 2021–December 2022, and the post-NPI period was January 2023–December 2025. Thirteen pathogen categories were analyzed using period comparisons, interrupted time-series models, and multivariable logistic regression incorporating meteorological factors, air quality index, and school-term status.ResultsOverall positivity was higher in the post-NPI period than in the NPI period (75.4% vs. 58.8%), and co-detection was also higher in the post-NPI period (15.2% vs. 6.0%). Pathogen-specific interrupted time-series analysis showed heterogeneous patterns: human adenovirus showed a robust immediate level decrease (−13.00 percentage points; 95% CI, −20.13 to −5.87; FDR-adjusted P = 0.005), whereas human rhinovirus showed a significant positive trend change after the January 2023 interruption (+1.07 percentage points per month; 95% CI, 0.63–1.50; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001), with a positive post-NPI slope (+0.64 percentage points per month). Higher temperature was associated with lower positivity of human respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus, and influenza B virus, but higher positivity of human parainfluenza virus and human bocavirus. School-term status was associated with higher human rhinovirus positivity (aOR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.34–2.52; FDR-adjusted P = 0.002).ConclusionThe NPI and post-NPI periods showed distinct and heterogeneous temporal patterns in pediatric respiratory pathogen detection.
